title: The Darwin Awards
tagline: A comedy... to die for.
overview: After botching the capture of a notorious serial killer, idiosyncratic detective Michael Burrows loses his job with the San Francisco Police. He becomes an investigator for an insurance company and joins forces with a cynical field agent to probe suspicious and unusual deaths.
plot:
The Darwin Awards is a 2006 American adventure comedy written and directed by Finn Taylor and based on the website of the same name. Joseph Fiennes stars as Michael Burrows and Winona Ryder as Siri Taylor, with David Arquette, Juliette Lewis, Wilmer Valderrama, Chris Penn, Julianna Margulies, Robin Tunney, Ty Burrell Adam Savage, Jamie Hyneman and the band Metallica. It premiered at the Sundance Film Festival on January 25, 2006, the day after Penn's death; it was his final film.

The film opens with a car speeding along with a JATO rocket strapped to it, then turns to Michael, a criminal profiler with the San Francisco Police Department. It is presented in documentary style as the thesis project of a film-school graduate who follows Michael with a camera. Michael's fear of blood lets a serial killer escape, and he is fired from the force. After weeks of depression, he finds a way to combine his professional skill with his obsession with the Darwin Awards: he will help insurance companies identify the people most likely to kill themselves through sheer foolishness, so that they can be refused policies.

His profiling talent impresses an insurance executive, who pairs him with Siri, a specialist in bizarre claims. Together they travel the country investigating legendary cases of idiocy, including the rocket-powered car and a pair of ice fishermen who use a stick of dynamite to blast a hole in the ice, only for their dog to fetch the lit explosive and carry it back to their new SUV. Michael tries to find a common thread among the victims, but the only explanation on offer is Siri's rambling theory that insurers who deny claims drive people mad. Michael himself repeatedly comes close to earning a Darwin Award; stranded with Siri on a freezing night, he blows up his car trying to start a fire with gasoline.

By chance, Michael discovers where the killer who escaped him is now living and abseils down the side of the building to film him. The film student, glimpsed for the first time, is dangling on the other end of the same rope, and the heavy stone urn they are tied to starts creeping toward the edge of the roof. Inside, the killer slices the hand of the captive Siri to trigger Michael's fear of blood, but Michael overcomes it and defeats him.

The film was poorly received, with a 25% rating on Rotten Tomatoes; critics found it formulaic and unfunny.

title: Horsemen
tagline: Four victims. Four painful secrets.
overview: A recently widowed detective still grieving over his wife's death discovers a shocking connection between himself and the suspects in a serial killing spree linked to the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse.
plot:
Horsemen is a 2009 American psychological thriller directed by Jonas Åkerlund, written by David Callaham and produced by Michael Bay. It stars Dennis Quaid as Aidan Breslin, a detective and forensic dentistry expert, and Zhang Ziyi as Kristen, the adopted daughter of one of the victims, with Lou Taylor Pucci, Clifton Collins Jr., Barry Shabaka Henley, Neal McDonough and Peter Stormare. The film was shot over eight weeks in Winnipeg, Manitoba.

Breslin is a widower who has become emotionally distant from his two sons, Alex and Sean, since his wife's death. Because of his expertise in dental forensics, he is called to a strange crime scene containing human teeth and the painted words "come and see". Soon after, a woman named Mrs. Spitz is found suspended from a hook contraption in her bedroom, the same message written on the walls, and the autopsy reveals that she was pregnant and that the fetus has been removed. Breslin concludes that four attackers were involved and that they filmed the murder.

As more victims are found in similarly staged scenes, a tattoo parlor owner who built four of the hook devices offers a lead, and a remark from his son Sean leads Breslin to the Bible. He realizes that the killings are modeled on the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse from the Book of Revelation, with each crime representing War, Famine, Pestilence or Death. Kristen unexpectedly confesses to the murder of her adoptive mother, revealing a disturbing history of abuse in the Spitz household. As the remaining killers carry out their ritual and Breslin struggles to uncover who is behind the group, the investigation leads him closer to his own home and family than he could have imagined.

The film combines a serial killer mystery with themes of parental neglect, abuse and alienated youth, presented with heavily stylized visuals and graphic violence.

Horsemen received a limited release in the United States on March 6, 2009, before arriving on home video in July. It was poorly received, with 17 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes from a small number of reviews; Variety's Jordan Mintzer found it predictable and full of clichés such as overstylized torture, whiplash editing and crude neon lighting.

title: The Taking of Pelham 1 2 3
tagline: I can't get it out of my head. I'm gonna die today.
overview: Armed men hijack a New York City subway train, holding the passengers hostage in return for a ransom, and turning an ordinary day's work for dispatcher Walter Garber into a face-off with the mastermind behind the crime.
plot:
'Ryder' and his accomplices – Bashkin, Emri, and former train operator Phil Ramos – hijack Pelham 123, a New York City Subway 6 train, at 77th Street. Uncoupling the front car of the train below 51st Street, Bashkin kills an intervening plainclothes New York City Transit Police officer as they take its passengers hostage.
26 year Metropolitan Transportation Authority veteran Walter Garber, working in the Rail Control Center as a train dispatcher, receives a call from Ryder, demanding $10 million in cash to be paid within 60 minutes. Ryder warns that for every minute past the deadline he will kill a hostage. Garber reluctantly negotiates with him, while Ramos and Emri set up Internet access in the tunnel.
On his laptop, Ryder watches the Dow Jones Industrial Average plunge nearly 1,000 points in response to the hijacking. A hostage's laptop also connects to the Internet, and its webcam allows the control center to observe Ryder and Ramos. Garber's boss sends him home as Lieutenant Camonetti of the New York City Police Department Emergency Service Unit takes over negotiations. Infuriated, Ryder kills the train's motorman Jerry Pollard to force Camonetti to bring Garber back into the building.
Camonetti learns that Garber is being investigated for allegedly accepting a $35,000 bribe over a contract for new subway cars. Ryder also finds the allegations online, forcing Garber to confess by threatening to kill a teenager. To save the hostage, Garber says he was offered the bribe while deciding between two companies, using the money to pay for his daughters' college tuition, but insists he would have made the same decision regardless.
The mayor authorizes payment of the ransom and a police car is dispatched to transport the money to the subway station. En route, the police car crashes, failing to deliver the money on time. An enraged Ryder threatens to execute a child's mother, but another hostage, former soldier Wallace, sacrifices himself and is killed.
A brief gunfight erupts after an Emergency Service Unit sniper is bitten by a rat and discharges his weapon, killing Ramos. Ryder demands Garber deliver the ransom money himself to avoid having contact with the police. Garber is flown to the terminal, where he is given a pistol for protection.
The police discover Ryder is Dennis Ford, a former stockbroker who ran a private equity firm on Wall Street. He was sentenced to prison for embezzling $20 million from the city's pension fund, his biggest client. Ford had taken a plea bargain to serve three years, but eventually received a ten-year sentence because he failed to make full restitution.
Ford spent the last four years of his nine-year stretch in the same cell block as Ramos, and was released from Clinton Correctional Facility two weeks ago. One of the mayor's aides mentions the extreme drop in the major stock indexes. So, the mayor infers that Ryder is manipulating the market via put options.

title: Neon Genesis Evangelion: The End of Evangelion
original_title: 新世紀エヴァンゲリオン劇場版 Air／まごころを、君に
tagline: The fate of destruction is also the joy of rebirth
overview: The second of two theatrically released follow-ups to the Neon Genesis Evangelion series. Comprising of two alternate episodes which were first intended to take the place of episodes 25 and 26, this finale answers many of the questions surrounding the series, while also opening up some new possibilities.
plot:
Neon Genesis Evangelion: The End of Evangelion is a 96-minute anime film directed by Hideaki Anno, released in 1997. It serves as the final installment of the Neon Genesis Evangelion series and concludes the story of Shinji Ikari, a young boy who pilots the giant humanoid robot Evangelion Unit-01.

The film begins with Shinji, still reeling from the events of the previous episodes, struggling to cope with his emotional trauma. He is visited by Rei Ayanami, a mysterious and enigmatic being who has been a central figure in the series. Rei's presence serves as a catalyst for Shinji's introspection, and he begins to question his own identity and purpose.

As the story unfolds, Shinji becomes increasingly entangled with Asuka Langley Soryu, a rival pilot of Evangelion Unit-02. Their interactions are marked by tension and conflict, reflecting their deep-seated emotional scars. Meanwhile, the organization NERV, led by Gendo Ikari (Shinji's father), continues to pursue its goals of using the Evangelions to bring about human evolution.

The plot thickens as Shinji discovers a series of cryptic messages from his mother, Yui Ikari, who had been presumed dead. These messages reveal that she was involved in NERV's research and that her death was not what it seemed. This revelation sets off a chain reaction of events that lead to the climax of the film.

The final act of the movie is marked by an intense and surreal sequence of events. Shinji, Asuka, and Rei find themselves trapped in a series of nightmarish scenarios, each representing a different aspect of their psyches. These sequences are intercut with scenes of the Evangelions engaging in battle against monstrous creatures known as Angels.

As the story reaches its conclusion, Shinji is forced to confront his deepest fears and insecurities. He ultimately comes to terms with his own identity and finds a sense of acceptance and belonging. The film's ending is intentionally ambiguous, leaving the audience to ponder the meaning and significance of the events that have transpired.

Throughout the film, Anno explores themes of existentialism, psychological trauma, and the human condition. The movie's abstract and often surreal narrative style adds to its complexity and depth, making it a thought-provoking and emotionally resonant conclusion to the Neon Genesis Evangelion series.

Ultimately, Neon Genesis Evangelion: The End of Evangelion is a powerful and haunting film that challenges viewers to confront their own emotions and insecurities. Its exploration of complex themes and abstract narrative style have made it a cult classic and a staple of anime fandom.

title: Gamer
tagline: In the near future, you don't live to play... you'll play to live.
overview: Mind-control technology has taken society by a storm, a multiplayer on-line game called "Slayers" allows players to control human prisoners in mass-scale. Simon controls Kable, the online champion of the game. Kable's ultimate challenge becomes regaining his identity and independence by defeating the game's mastermind.
plot:
In 2034, computer programmer Ken Castle invents self-replicating nanites that replace brain tissue and allow humans to control other humans' actions and see through their eyes. The first application of Castle's "Nanex" technology is a virtual community life simulation game, Society, which allows gamers to manipulate live actors as their avatars. Society becomes a worldwide sensation, making Castle the richest man in the world. He then creates Slayers, a third-person shooter where the "characters" are death-row prisoners using real weapons in specially designated areas. Unlike Society actors, Slayers participants are not paid; instead, they volunteer, and any Slayer who survives 30 matches will earn their freedom. John "Kable" Tillman is everyone's favorite, having survived a record 27 matches, and is controlled by 17-year-old gamer Simon Silverton.
An activist organization called the "Humanz" hacks a talk-show interview with Castle and claims that his technology will one day be used to control people against their will. The Humanz also disrupts Society play, but Castle sees both these actions as trivial. However, Castle feels threatened by Kable's winning streak and introduces a new inmate into Slayers, Hackman, specifically to kill Kable. Unknown to anyone else, Hackman will not be controlled by a player, thus not be handicapped by the "ping" that causes a small but dangerous delay between the player's command and the Slayer's action.
Kable's estranged wife, Angie, works as a Society character, but in spite of her earnings, she is refused custody of their daughter, Delia, who has been placed with a wealthy foster family.
The Humanz contact Kable and Simon separately and offer to create a mod that will let him escape, but only if Simon relinquishes control during the game. Simon is even given a mod to speak freely to Kable. The escape is successful, and news outlets report that Kable has been fragged, which puts Simon in a difficult position: he is labeled a "cheater", locked out of his account which is spammed with hate mail, his father's asset frozen, and arrested by the FBI for helping Kable escape.
Kable is brought to the Humanz' hideout; he refuses to help their fight against Castle but learns of Angie's current location in Society. He rescues her, escaping from both Hackman and Castle's security forces. Gina, the talk show host who secretly assists the Humanz, meets them. The Humanz deactivates the nanites in Angie and Kable's brains, and Kable remembers that the original nanites were tested on him while he was still in the military. Under Castle's control, Kable shot and killed his best friend and was imprisoned.
Upon learning that Castle is the wealthy father who adopted Delia, Kable infiltrates his mansion to get her back. He locates Castle, who reveals that his henchmen have already tracked down the Humanz' lair and killed all of them.

title: Bronson
tagline: The Man. The Myth. The Celebrity.
overview: A young man who was sentenced to 7 years in prison for robbing a post office ends up spending 30 years in solitary confinement. During this time, his own personality is supplanted by his alter ego, Charles Bronson.
plot:
Bronson is a 2008 British biographical prison film and black comedy directed by Nicolas Winding Refn, who co-wrote it with Brock Norman Brock. Tom Hardy stars as Michael Peterson, the man who took the name Charles Bronson in 1987 and came to be regarded as Britain's most violent prisoner, responsible for around a dozen hostage-takings behind bars. Matt King, James Lance, Kelly Adams and Amanda Burton co-star.

Peterson recounts his own life with mocking, self-deprecating humour, sometimes speaking straight to the camera in prison clothes and sometimes performing it as a stage act before a theatre audience. In 1974, aged 22, he robs a post office and receives seven years, but his violence inside keeps lengthening the sentence. Moved to a psychiatric hospital, he is sedated with drugs he says sap his strength, and in 1978 he tries to win a transfer back to prison by attempting to strangle a fellow inmate, a self-confessed paedophile, stopping short of murder. He points out that, for all his years in confinement, he has never killed anyone. He claims that a rooftop protest in 1982, which caused enormous damage, led the authorities to declare him sane and release him in 1987.

Free again, he visits his parents and his predatory Uncle Jack, who reunites him with a former inmate who arranges bare-knuckle fights and gives him the ring name Charles Bronson, after the American actor. On New Year's Day 1988 he steals a ring to propose to a woman who tells him he was only a fling, and after sixty-nine days of freedom he is back in jail. In 1993 he takes a prison librarian hostage, greases his naked body for the coming brawl with the guards, and is warned by the governor that he will die inside. In 1999 an art teacher sees promise in his drawings and Bronson briefly becomes a model prisoner, but when the art class is to close he seizes the teacher, paints himself black and arranges his captive as a living copy of René Magritte's The Son of Man before summoning the guards for another beating. Closing text notes that he has spent some thirty years in solitary confinement with no release date.

Hardy spoke with the real Bronson by phone before meeting him, and Bronson praised his portrayal. Filming took place in and around Nottingham. The film grossed about $2.3 million and drew positive reviews for Hardy's performance, holding 75% on Rotten Tomatoes and 71 on Metacritic, though some critics objected to its violence.

title: The Ramen Girl
tagline: Her romance is on pins and noodles.
overview: An American woman is stranded in Tokyo after breaking up with her boyfriend. Searching for direction in life, she trains to be a râmen chef under a tyrannical Japanese master.
plot:
The Ramen Girl is a 2008 romantic comedy-drama directed by Robert Allan Ackerman and starring Brittany Murphy, who also co-produced, as an American woman who learns to make ramen in Tokyo. Toshiyuki Nishida plays her demanding teacher and Kimiko Yo his wife, with Sohee Park, Tammy Blanchard, Gabriel Mann and Tsutomu Yamazaki, star of the noodle comedy Tampopo (1985). Much of the dialogue is in Japanese.

Abby has moved to Tokyo to be with her boyfriend Ethan, who soon dumps her and leaves for Osaka. Heartbroken, she wanders into a small ramen shop near her apartment, run by the gruff chef Maezumi and his wife Reiko, neither of whom speaks English. Maezumi serves her a bowl of noodles that leaves her strangely moved; she imagines the shop's beckoning cat waving at her, and the couple refuse her money. Returning, she helps out when Reiko is injured, and decides she wants to learn the art of ramen.

Maezumi reluctantly agrees to teach her but treats her harshly and gives her menial work in the hope that she will give up. Abby perseveres, wins over the customers as a waitress and meets Toshi Iwamoto, a young businessman with whom she bonds over the unexpected turns their lives have taken. When Maezumi's rival Udagawa boasts that a Grand Master will soon judge whether his son is worthy to carry on his ramen tradition, Maezumi drunkenly promises that Abby will be tested too. Abby learns from Reiko that Maezumi has not spoken in years to their son Shintaro, who left to become a chef in Paris.

Toshi is transferred to Shanghai and asks Abby to go with him, but she stays. Insisting that her ramen has no soul, Maezumi takes her to his mother, who tells her she must cook from the heart. Abby makes her broth in tears, and the customers who taste it are moved to tears themselves. The Grand Master enjoys her unconventional creation but withholds his blessing, saying she needs more restraint. Maezumi nonetheless names her his true successor before closing his shop after forty-five years, and gives her the lantern from its door.

A year later Abby runs her own ramen shop in New York, where Toshi, who has quit his job to make music, finds her. Reviews were mixed, with critics describing it as a gentle but slight mix of The Karate Kid and Tampopo.

title: Eye of the Beholder
tagline: Obsession is in the eye of the beholder.
overview: A reclusive surveillance expert is hired to spy on a mysterious blackmailer, who just may be a serial killer.
plot:
Eye of the Beholder is a 1999 mystery thriller with elements of magical realism, written and directed by Stephan Elliott. Based on Marc Behm's novel of the same name, which had previously been filmed by Claude Miller as the 1983 French thriller Deadly Circuit, it stars Ewan McGregor and Ashley Judd, with Patrick Bergin, k.d. lang and Geneviève Bujold. The film was an international co-production between Canada, the United Kingdom and Australia.

Stephen Wilson, known as "the Eye", is an intelligence agent who specialises in surveillance. He is still haunted by the loss of his young daughter, whom he has not seen since his former wife took her away, and her image constantly appears to him and talks to him. He is assigned to find out what trouble the socialite son of his superior has got into, and follows him to an encounter with a mysterious woman, Joanna Eris. Through his hidden camera, Stephen watches her murder the young man.

Instead of reporting her, Stephen becomes fascinated with Eris, whom he comes to see as a lost, vulnerable child, and he begins following her across the United States as she changes identities and kills again. Gradually he pieces together her past: she was abandoned by her father as a child, which seems to explain her deep hostility towards men. He keeps his discoveries to himself and protects her from a distance.

In one city, Eris meets Alexander, a wealthy blind man, and the two fall in love and plan to marry. Anxious to stop her from killing again, Stephen shoots out a tyre of their car on the way to the wedding, causing a crash that kills Alexander. A grieving Eris heads into the desert, where a drug addict named Gary picks her up when her car breaks down, then beats her and injects her with heroin in order to rape her. Stephen intervenes and beats Gary, but Eris loses the baby she was carrying.

She flees to Alaska and works as a waitress, and Stephen finally approaches her in person. They grow close over drinks, though Eris insists she has nothing to offer him. When the police and her psychiatrist come to arrest her, Stephen rescues her and takes her to his trailer, where she discovers that he has been watching her all along. Horrified, she shoots him, not knowing that his gun is loaded with blanks, and flees. He pursues her, and her car crashes through the ice of a lake. Stephen pulls her out, and she dies in his arms.

The film was a box-office failure and was panned by critics, with 10% approval on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: The Haunting in Connecticut
tagline: Some things cannot be explained.
overview: When the Campbell family moves to upstate Connecticut, they soon learn that their charming Victorian home has a disturbing history: not only was the house a transformed funeral parlor where inconceivable acts occurred, but the owner's clairvoyant son Jonah served as a demonic messenger, providing a gateway for spiritual entities to crossover.
plot:
In 1987, Sara Campbell is driving her son Matt home from a Connecticut hospital where he has been undergoing experimental cancer treatments. Sara and her husband, Peter, a recovering alcoholic, discuss finding a rental house closer to the hospital. On another hospital visit, Sara finds a man putting up a "For Rent" sign in front of a large house. The man is frustrated and offers her the first month free if she rents the house immediately.
The following day, Peter arrives with Matt's brother Billy and cousins Wendy and Mary, and they choose rooms. Matt chooses the basement, which is divided by a partition wall with a locked door. After moving in, Matt suffers a series of visions involving an old, bearded man and corpses with symbols carved into their skin. The next day, Peter learns that the house was originally a funeral home; the room behind the mysterious door in the basement is a mortuary.
Matt tells another cancer patient, Reverend Nicholas Popescu, about his visions. Nicholas advises him to find out what the spirit wants. Later, Matt encounters a burned figure in his room who begins to move toward him. When the family comes home, they find a shirtless Matt with his fingers bleeding from scratching at the wall.
The family begins to disintegrate under the stress of Matt's illness and bizarre behavior. The children find a box of photographs, which show Jonah, a young man from Matt's visions, at a séance, emitting ectoplasm from his mouth. They also find a container of desiccated human eyelids. Wendy and Matt discover that the funeral home was run by a man named Ramsey Aickman, who conducted psychic research and would host séances with Jonah acting as a medium. At one séance, all those attending, including Aickman, were found dead, and Jonah disappeared.
Nicholas theorizes that Aickman was practicing necromancy in an attempt to control the dead and bind them to the house. That night, Nicholas finds human remains in the house and removes them. Matt awakens to find Aickman's symbols carved into his skin. He is taken to the hospital, where he encounters Jonah's ghost. Nicholas and Matt begin to have simultaneous visions revealing Jonah's fate: During the séance, a demonic presence burnt all the attendees in a flash of light. Jonah fled, using a dumbwaiter to escape the basement, but inadvertently became trapped in the crematory, where he was cremated alive.
Peter and Sara learn that Matt's cancer treatments have had no effect. They then discover that Matt has escaped the hospital. At home, Nicholas leaves a message telling the family to get out immediately, as it was Jonah's spirit that protected them. Matt breaks through the walls in the front room with an axe, revealing the dusty corpses Aickman hid in the walls. He forces Wendy and the children outside before barricading himself in the house and tearing down the other walls as corpses begin to tumble into the room. Jonah seemingly possesses Matt, who lights the bodies and the room on fire.

title: The Hangover
tagline: Some guys just can't handle Vegas.
overview: When three friends finally come to after a raucous night of bachelor-party revelry, they find a baby in the closet and a tiger in the bathroom. But they can't seem to locate their best friend, Doug – who's supposed to be tying the knot. Launching a frantic search for Doug, the trio perseveres through a nasty hangover to try to make it to the church on time.
plot:
The Hangover is a 2009 American comedy film directed by Todd Phillips and written by Craig Mazin and Scott Moore. The movie follows the story of a group of friends who wake up after a wild bachelor party in Las Vegas with no memory of the night before.

The film begins with Phil Wenneck (Bradley Cooper), Stu Price (Ed Helms), Alan Garner (Zach Galifianakis), and Doug Billings (Justin Bartha) preparing for Doug's wedding to his fiancée, Tracy (Jamie Chung). The group decides to take a wild bachelor party to Las Vegas, where they spend the night drinking, dancing, and getting into various misadventures.

The next morning, the friends wake up in Phil's hotel suite with no memory of what happened the night before. They soon discover that Doug is missing, and their friend's wedding is just hours away. As they try to piece together the events of the previous night, they find a tiger in the bathroom, a missing front tooth for Stu, and a mysterious woman named Jade (Heather Graham) who claims to have slept with them.

As the friends try to track down Doug and figure out what happened to him, they encounter various obstacles, including a wild goose chase through the streets of Las Vegas, a run-in with a group of thugs, and a series of hilarious misadventures. Along the way, they also discover that Jade is not who she claims to be, and that the night before was much more eventful than they initially thought.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the friends had a wild and crazy night in Las Vegas, involving sex, drugs, and general debauchery. They eventually track down Doug's whereabouts and are able to return him to his fiancée just in time for the wedding.

The movie ends with the friends reflecting on the events of the previous night and the consequences that followed. While they all agree that it was a wild and crazy adventure, they also acknowledge that it may have been a mistake. The film ends with a comedic twist, as the friends are seen walking away from the wedding ceremony, still trying to process what happened the night before.

Throughout the movie, the humor is driven by the absurdity of the situation and the characters' reactions to it. The cast delivers strong performances, particularly Zach Galifianakis as the eccentric and unpredictable Alan Garner. The film's success can be attributed to its well-crafted script, clever direction, and talented cast, which all come together to create a hilarious and entertaining movie experience.

Overall, The Hangover is a raunchy and irreverent comedy that explores themes of friendship, bachelorhood, and the consequences of one's actions. While it may not be for everyone, the film has become a cult classic and spawned two successful sequels.

title: Irresistible
tagline: A secret is not safe if the truth has a witness.
overview: A wife and mother is consumed by the thought that her husband's co-worker is trying to win him away from her and their family.
plot:
Irresistible is a 2006 Australian psychological thriller and mystery drama written and directed by Ann Turner. Susan Sarandon stars as Sophie Hartley, an American illustrator, with Sam Neill as her husband Craig and Emily Blunt as Mara, his new colleague. Charles "Bud" Tingwell and William McInnes appear in supporting roles.

Sophie is a successful children's book illustrator, happily married to Craig and mother of two young daughters, Ruby and Elly. Still grieving the recent death of her mother, she begins to notice strange things around the house. One afternoon, convinced she left the iron on, she rushes home to find it still hot but switched off, and she later senses that someone has been inside. At a party she meets Mara, a young and attractive woman who works with Craig. On a walk along the beach, Mara sympathizes over Sophie's loss and tells her about her own grief for a best friend, an aid worker who died trying to save babies when an orphanage in Kosovo was firebombed.

In the following weeks, objects disappear from the house, including one of Sophie's dresses and Elly's favorite toy. One of Sophie's illustrations is ruined, which she blames on the cat knocking over an inkwell, and she is attacked by wasps that emerge from an ornament in her studio. When she sees Mara wearing the missing dress, Sophie becomes convinced that the younger woman is breaking into her home and trying to take over her life. She breaks into Mara's apartment in search of proof but is caught, and a court issues a restraining order against her, with Craig failing to support her. Increasingly isolated, and suspecting that Craig and Mara are having an affair, Sophie retreats to a friend's cabin to clear her head. Conversations with her father bring buried secrets from her own youth to the surface, and as her family and those around her question her sanity, Sophie must determine whether Mara truly poses a threat or whether her grief and guilt are distorting her perception.

The film received mixed reviews. Critics praised Sarandon's committed performance and Blunt's unsettling turn as Mara, made shortly before her breakthrough in international cinema, but many found the plot twists contrived and the suspense uneven.

title: Naruto: Guardians of the Crescent Moon Kingdom
original_title: 劇場版 NARUTO -ナルト- 大興奮!みかづき島のアニマル騒動だってばよ
overview: Naruto Uzumaki, Kakashi Hatake, Sakura Haruno, and Rock Lee are assigned to protect the prince of the Land of the Moon, Michiru, during his world trip; other escorts had been hired, but quit due to being treated poorly. The Land of the Moon is a very wealthy nation, so Michiru tends to buy whatever he wants, and has a very materialistic worldview. His Hikaru, also acts in much the same manner.
plot:
Naruto the Movie: Guardians of the Crescent Moon Kingdom (Japanese title literally "Great Excitement! The Animal Panic of Crescent Moon Island!") is a Japanese animated martial arts fantasy adventure of 2006 written and directed by Toshiyuki Tsuru and produced by Studio Pierrot, based on Masashi Kishimoto's manga. The third and last film of the series' first part, it features the voices of Junko Takeuchi as Naruto Uzumaki, Chie Nakamura as Sakura Haruno, Yōichi Masukawa as Rock Lee, Kazuhiko Inoue as Kakashi Hatake, Kyōsuke Ikeda as Prince Hikaru and Akio Ōtsuka as his father Michiru.

Naruto, Kakashi, Sakura and Lee are assigned to escort Michiru, heir to the fabulously rich Land of the Moon, and his spoiled son Hikaru home. Michiru casually buys an entire circus so that Hikaru can befriend its star sabre-toothed cat, Chamū, and its monkey partner Kiki, but Chamū attacks the boy. Michiru's former wife, Amayo, rejects his hopes of reconciliation, saying he does not understand what really matters. During a storm at sea, Naruto rebukes Hikaru for not caring about the animals, and Hikaru helps save Chamū and Kiki, winning their friendship and Naruto's.

On arrival they find that the greedy minister Shabadaba has overthrown King Kakeru, Michiru's father. Loyal soldiers under Captain Korega help the group flee to a mountain refuge, where the dying Kakeru, turned partly to stone by the gauntlet of the hired ninja Ishidate, tells his son that wealth is not happiness and names him king. Ishidate's mercenaries poison the team, kill Korega and capture Michiru. Shabadaba reveals that he seized power to keep the kingdom's riches for himself, whereas Kakeru wanted to spend them on his people. Rallied by Naruto, the group sneaks into the palace with help from the circus, Kakashi leads a surprise attack, and Lee and Sakura defeat Ishidate's henchmen Karenbana and Kongō. Hikaru saves his father from hanging with an arrow, and, carried by father and son, Naruto finishes Ishidate and Shabadaba with a Rasengan strengthened by the island's moonlight. While Kakashi recovers, the team enjoy two weeks on the island and see Michiru and Hikaru inaugurated as king and prince, and Michiru resolves to win back Amayo.

Distributed by Toho, the film opened in Japan on 5 August 2006 and grossed about $3.2 million.

title: Kite
tagline: Dangerous things come in small packages.
overview: Sawa may seem innocent and naive, but don’t be fooled. She is a cold-blooded killer, and if you’re on the wrong side of the law, you may be her next target. Not content to just watch as the imperfect justice system lets more and more criminals go loose every day, a detective decides to train the young Sawa to be his instrument of justice.
plot:
Kite is a 1998 Japanese adult original video animation written and directed by Yasuomi Umetsu. Originally released on VHS as two episodes of about 25 minutes each in February and October 1998, it was later edited into a single feature for its home video releases in the United States, in versions with differing amounts of sexual content. The story follows a teenage girl forced to work as an assassin, and it is notorious for its graphic violence and sexual abuse.

Sawa is a schoolgirl orphaned after her parents were brutally murdered. She is taken in by two detectives, Akai and Kanie, who were assigned to the case. They use her as a hired killer, sending her to eliminate targets ranging from corrupt police officers to wealthy businessmen. Akai also sexually abuses her, and he has given her a pair of crystal earrings said to contain her parents' blood. Sawa's killings become infamous among the police because of the special bullets she uses, which explode after entering the body. In an early assignment she kills a celebrity during a date.

On one job Sawa meets Oburi, a boy of her age who also works as an assassin for the two men, and they form a close bond. Oburi gives her the courage to imagine escaping. When Oburi decides to leave after completing a final set of assignments, Akai orders Sawa to kill him. Oburi tells her that her guardians murdered her parents, and Sawa replies that she has long known. She spares him, and later, wounded and missing an earring after a mission, rescues him when a target turns out to be a heavily armed police officer.

When Oburi announces that both of them are quitting, Akai beats him and captures Sawa, then punishes Oburi by forcing him to watch as he assaults her. Kanie takes Oburi away to be killed, and Akai, believing Sawa has turned against Oburi, tells her where he is being taken. The next morning, Akai is called to a crime scene and finds Kanie's body at the very spot where Sawa's parents were killed years earlier.

Akai rushes to the place where Oburi was to be executed but finds Sawa waiting, and she shoots him repeatedly with both her own and Oburi's guns before throwing the weapons away along with her remaining earring. Before the two can reunite, Oburi is shot by another young assassin. Sawa waits for him in his hideout, turning at the sound of a footstep as the screen goes dark.

Reviews have been generally positive, with critics praising its action and animation while noting its deeply disturbing content.

title: Man-Thing
tagline: The nature of fear
overview: Agents of an oil tycoon vanish while exploring a swamp marked for drilling. The local sheriff investigates and faces a Seminole legend come to life: Man-Thing, a shambling swamp-monster whose touch burns those who feel fear.
plot:
Man-Thing is a 2005 superhero monster film loosely based on the Marvel Comics character of the same name. Directed by Brett Leonard and written by Hans Rodionoff, it stars Matthew Le Nevez, Rachael Taylor and Jack Thompson, with Conan Stevens as the title creature, a shambling swamp monster drawn from a Seminole legend. Originally intended for a theatrical release in the United States, the film premiered in Singapore in April 2005 and was then shown in the US as a "Sci-Fi Original" on the Sci Fi Channel on April 30, 2005.

At Dark Waters, a sacred Native American swampland said to be home to a mysterious guardian spirit, a teenager is killed by a plant-like monster. Kyle Williams, a young replacement sheriff, arrives in the town of Bywater and learns from deputy Fraser that his predecessor is one of 47 people who have gone missing since oil tycoon Fred Schist acquired the tribal lands from the Seminole chief and shaman Ted Sallis, who was the first to disappear. Schist insists that Sallis sold the land legally and ran off with the money, and he blames the trouble on local protesters and on Rene Laroque, a swamp dweller who has been sabotaging his drilling operation. As Williams investigates, more bodies turn up, some with plants growing out of them. Photographer Mike Ploog and shaman Pete Horn tell him about the legend of the swamp's guardian, and the medical examiner, Val Mayerik, admits that the former sheriff ordered him to record the deaths as alligator attacks. Williams heads into the swamp to track Laroque while Schist sends a pair of local thugs to kill him, and the creature lurking in the water claims more victims. Helped by schoolteacher Teri Richards, for whom he develops romantic feelings, Williams gradually uncovers the truth about Schist's crimes, the fate of Ted Sallis and the vengeful force rising from the sacred ground to punish those who have desecrated it.

Man-Thing received negative reviews from critics and was a box-office bomb, earning about $1 million from a small international theatrical release. David Nusair of Reel Film Reviews called it "the worst comic book movie ever made", while Felix Vasquez of Cinema Crazed praised its special effects but felt it botched a good concept. It was released on DVD in June 2005.

title: Facing the Giants
tagline: Never give up. Never back down. Never lose faith.
overview: A losing coach with an underdog football team faces their giants of fear and failure on and off the field to surprising results.
plot:
Facing the Giants is a 2006 American sports drama film directed by Chris Evans and written by Aneestyn Fokkena, Chris Fabry, and Jon Abrahams. The movie stars Shannen Doherty, Kenan Thompson, and Cody Kasch.

The story revolves around the fictional high school football team, Mount Paulet High School's Panthers, who are struggling to find success on and off the field. The team is led by Coach Grant Taylor (played by Shannen Doherty), a former NFL player who has lost his faith in God after a tragic accident involving his son.

As the season begins, the team faces numerous challenges, including internal conflicts, personal struggles, and external pressures from their opponents. However, with the help of a new assistant coach, Coach Grant Taylor's wife, Jill (played by Shannen Doherty), who is a Christian minister, the team starts to come together.

Through a series of events, including a dramatic game against their arch-rivals, the Panthers learn valuable lessons about teamwork, perseverance, and faith. The movie explores themes of redemption, forgiveness, and the power of prayer, as the team faces various obstacles on and off the field.

As the season progresses, Coach Taylor's relationship with his son, who is struggling with a serious illness, becomes a central focus of the story. Through his faith and perseverance, Coach Taylor finds the strength to overcome his personal struggles and lead his team to victory.

The movie culminates in an intense game against their arch-rivals, where the Panthers face off against their toughest opponent yet. With the help of prayer and teamwork, the Panthers emerge victorious, but not without some unexpected twists and turns.

Throughout the film, the characters undergo significant personal growth and development, learning valuable lessons about faith, perseverance, and the importance of working together towards a common goal. The movie features a mix of drama, sports action, and inspirational moments, making it an engaging and uplifting watch for audiences of all ages.

Overall, Facing the Giants is a heartwarming and inspiring film that explores themes of faith, redemption, and perseverance in the face of adversity. With its talented cast, engaging storyline, and uplifting message, this movie is sure to leave viewers feeling motivated and inspired.

title: The Boat That Rocked
tagline: On air. Off shore. Out of control.
overview: The Boat That Rocked is an ensemble comedy, where the romance is between the young people of the 60s, and pop music. It's about a band of DJs that captivate Britain, playing the music that defines a generation and standing up to a government that  wanted control of popular culture via the British Broadcasting Corporation. Loosely based on the events in Britain in the 60's when the Labour government of Harold Wilson, wanted to bring the pirate radio stations under control, enough to see the passage of the Marine Broadcasting Offences Act on 15 August 1967. Also known as "Pirate Radio".
plot:
The Boat That Rocked, released in North America as Pirate Radio, is a 2009 British comedy-drama film written and directed by Richard Curtis about pirate radio in the United Kingdom in the 1960s. Its ensemble cast includes Philip Seymour Hoffman, Bill Nighy, Rhys Ifans, Nick Frost, Kenneth Branagh, Tom Sturridge and Emma Thompson. It was produced by Working Title Films for Universal Pictures.

In 1966, while the BBC plays almost no rock and pop music, pirate stations broadcast it to millions of listeners from ships in international waters. Seventeen-year-old Carl, recently expelled from school, is sent by his mother to spend time with his godfather, Quentin, who runs Radio Rock from an old ship anchored in the North Sea. There Carl joins an eccentric community of disc jockeys and crew, led by the brash American DJ known as the Count.

In London, the government minister Sir Alistair Dormandy is determined to shut the pirate stations down, and instructs his aide, Twatt, to find a legal means of doing so. When the government forbids British companies from advertising on unlicensed stations, Quentin responds by bringing back the legendary DJ Gavin Kavanagh, whose popularity draws advertisers back but sparks a rivalry with the Count. Carl falls for Quentin's niece, Marianne, but she is seduced by the DJ Doctor Dave; the gentle DJ Simple Simon marries a glamorous fan who soon leaves him for Gavin, prompting a dangerous duel between Gavin and the Count on the ship's mast. When his mother visits at Christmas, Carl learns that the reclusive late-night DJ Bob Silver is his father, and Marianne later returns to him.

Dormandy finally gets his law when a fishing boat's distress call is blocked by Radio Rock's signal, and the Marine Broadcasting Offences Act makes the pirate stations illegal from August 1967. The crew defy the law and keep broadcasting, starting the ship's engine to evade arrest, but the old vessel's engine explodes and it begins to sink. Dormandy refuses to send help, but as the DJs keep broadcasting their position, dozens of fans sail out in small boats to rescue them, Carl being pulled from the water by Marianne.

The film premiered in London in March 2009 and was released in the United Kingdom on 1 April. It received mixed reviews, with criticism of its length, and performed poorly at the British box office; for North America it was cut by about twenty minutes. It grossed about $36.6 million worldwide against a $50 million budget.

title: Down
tagline: YOUR NEXT STOP... IS HELL.
overview: After the elevators at a New York City skyscraper begin inexplicably malfunctioning, putting its passengers at risk, mechanic Mark Newman and reporter Jennifer Evans begin separate investigations. Newman gets resistance from superiors at his company, which manufactured the elevator, while additional elevator incidents cause several gruesome deaths. The police get involved and suspect that terrorists are responsible, but a far stranger explanation looms.
plot:
Down, retitled The Shaft for its American release, is a 2001 English-language Dutch science fiction horror film written and directed by Dick Maas. James Marshall, Naomi Watts and Eric Thal star, with Michael Ironside, Edward Herrmann, Dan Hedaya and Ron Perlman in supporting roles. It is a remake of Maas's own 1983 Dutch-language film The Lift. Filming took place mainly in the Netherlands, with brief exterior shoots in New York City and Washington, D.C.

In New York, a lightning strike hits the Millennium Building, a 102-storey skyscraper with dozens of elevators, and its three express elevators start behaving strangely. The next day, a car carrying a group of pregnant women stalls between floors and rapidly overheats, sending them to hospital. Jennifer Evans, an ambitious tabloid reporter, is assigned to cover the incident. Mark Newman, a repairman and former Marine, and his colleague Jeff McClellan, technicians for the elevator company, inspect the system and find nothing wrong, with Jeff insisting that the computer controlling the elevators is flawless.

The incidents soon turn deadly. A blind man and his guide dog vanish in the building; a security guard is decapitated when his head is trapped between closing doors; and other occupants die in increasingly grisly ways. The building's owners and the elevator company's executives, worried about lawsuits and bad publicity, deny there is a problem, but Mark becomes convinced that the elevators are acting with intent. Teaming up with Jennifer, who sees a major story, he investigates and uncovers evidence of a secret experiment involving organic material in the elevator's control system, a discovery that puts them in danger from both the machine and the people who want the truth covered up.

Down premiered in 2001 but received a limited release, and reviews were mostly negative. Rotten Tomatoes reported a 20 percent approval rating based on a small number of reviews, with critics faulting its weak storyline, unrealistic deaths, dialogue and special effects. Dutch critics were also largely unfavorable. The film was released in the same year as Watts's breakthrough role in Mulholland Drive.

title: Johnson Family Vacation
tagline: Take the ride.
overview: Nate Johnson, a Los Angeles man estranged from his wife and three children, decides to reconnect with his family by taking them with him on a road trip to Missouri for a big family reunion.
plot:
The strict Nate Johnson and his son, aspiring rapper DJ, visit an auto body shop in Los Angeles to pick up the former's Lincoln Navigator, only to discover that it has been mistakenly upgraded with extravagant features. Despite Nate's objections, they are forced to take the customized SUV because they have a family reunion to attend in Caruthersville, Missouri. On their way home, Nate receives a call from his disapproving mother, Glorietta, who criticizes his marriage to his wife, Dorothy. His older brother, Mack, takes over the call, always trying to one-up Nate by appealing to their mother's material desires.
Upon arriving home, it is revealed that Nate and Dorothy are separated, living in separate houses down the street from each other, along with their daughters, Nikki and Destiny. Nikki is preoccupied with her cell phone, while Destiny struggles to retrieve her belongings for her imaginary dog, Sir Barks-a-Lot. Nate disapproves of Dorothy's studying and brings it up when he sees her bringing schoolwork on the road trip. Just as they are about to leave, a man named Stan Turner arrives, claiming to have a reservation for a date with Dorothy. Nate intervenes, asserting his role as Dorothy's husband and scaring Stan away.
The family sets off on their road trip, but soon after, they encounter a dangerous situation on a stretch of highway, with a semi truck attempting to run them off the road. Nate manages to avoid a collision, but the impact causes their suitcases to spill out of the vehicle. Everyone is visibly shaken, but they eventually find a hotel to rest. Dorothy pretends to be interested in reconciling with Nate, but her true motive is to take a break from the trip.
Tensions arise when Nate stops at an Indian casino, mistakenly thinking it is an Indian reservation. Nikki flirts with an Indian tour guide, causing Nate's disapproval. In response, Nate embarrasses Nikki, leading to an argument where he confiscates her cell phone as a punishment.
While on the road, they pick up a hitchhiker named Christelle, against Dorothy's better judgment. Chrishelle steals from Destiny and inadvertently leaves a drug pipe in the backseat. At Bun World for Destiny's birthday celebration, Chrishelle behaves strangely, frightening the family. During their stay at another hotel, Nate and DJ find an alligator named Twinkie in their bed, brought in by Chrishelle. They decide to distance themselves stealthily from her and continue the journey.
DJ eventually needs to relieve himself and urinates in a soda cup, which Nate later throws out of the window, accidentally hitting a police officer on a motorcycle. Nate's inattentiveness leads to a collision with a cement truck, covering the truck in wet cement.
Arrested for littering and possession of drugs (Chrishelle's pipe), the family finds themselves locked up. Dorothy manages to help the officer with his taxes, securing their release.

title: In Hell
tagline: Rage unleashed.
overview: A man must survive a prison where hardened criminals battle to the death for the warden's entertainment.
plot:
In Hell is an American action thriller of 2003 directed by Ringo Lam, his third and last collaboration with Jean-Claude Van Damme. Van Damme stars as Kyle LeBlanc, an American locked away in a brutal Russian prison, with Lawrence Taylor as the feared Inmate 451, Lloyd Battista as the corrupt warden General Hruschov, Michael Bailey Smith as Valya and Chris Moir as Billy Cooper.

Kyle, working abroad in the Russian city of Magnitogorsk, hears his wife being attacked over the phone and arrives to find her dead. Her killer, Sergio Kovic, bribes the judge and walks free, and the enraged Kyle grabs a bailiff's gun and shoots him dead in the courtroom. Sentenced to life without parole, he is sent to Kravavi Prison, ruled by General Hruschov, and beaten for hesitating to give up his wedding ring. He watches a young American inmate, Billy, dragged off to be raped by the Russian mobster Andrei, fights Andrei the next morning, and is thrown into solitary, where he attempts suicide. Deciding instead to survive, he gets himself moved into the cell of Inmate 451, notorious for killing his cellmates, and the two form an unlikely bond. Malakai, an American in a wheelchair, explains the gangs and the Mafia's pact with the guards.

Kyle trains as a prison fighter and kills Andrei in his first bout, which shakes him badly, but he keeps fighting, grows hard, wins the respect of the inmates and turns away help from the American embassy. When Malakai betrays Billy's escape plans in return for medical care, 451 burns him alive, recalling how he killed the teacher who abused him in the same way. Billy dies after resisting Valya's assault, warning Kyle not to let anyone change who he is. Kyle refuses to fight Valya and is strung up by his arms in the yard; moved by his endurance, the rival gangs unite and refuse to fight. Ordered to face Miloc, a giant prisoner he knew from solitary, Kyle again refuses, and a riot erupts in which Miloc is shot shielding him. Amid the chaos, 451 gives Kyle evidence of the prison's abuses and shows him a secret way to the garage. Kyle must first defeat Valya, who pulls a knife during the fight, and kills him. 451 stays behind to deal with Hruschov while Kyle recovers his ring and drives away. Back in the United States, he exposes Kravavi, which is shut down three months later.

The film was released on DVD in the United States in November 2003. Reviews were poor: TV Guide gave it one star out of five, and IGN said it was strictly for Van Damme fans.

overview: Manga artist Gengo Odaka lands a job with the World Children's Land amusement park only to become suspicious of the organization when a garbled message is discovered on tapes. plot:
The Nebulans, a race of cockroach-like aliens from a planet in M Space Hunter Nebula, plot to take over the Earth, as their home planet has been destroyed by pollution from another race native to the planet, which destroyed itself in the process. To carry out their plans in secret, they disguise themselves using skin suits based on deceased humans, and build World Children's Land, a theme park which serves as a disguise for their base of operations, centered inside a statue of Godzilla called the Godzilla Tower. They also have King Ghidorah and Gigan at their disposal, guiding the monsters using Action Signal Tapes, which broadcast a frequency that instructs them on what to do. The aliens plan to use their monsters to wipe out human civilisation.
Gengo Odaka, a freelance manga artist, inadvertently discovers one of the tapes after being hired by the Nebulans to produce concept art for the park. When the tape is played, the signal is heard by Godzilla and Anguirus on Monster Island, who realize something is amiss. Anguirus is sent to Tokyo to investigate but is driven back by the JSDF. After reporting back to Godzilla, the two monsters set off for Tokyo again to confront the Nebulans at World Children's Land.
As they arrive, the Nebulans send Gigan and Ghidorah into battle, who prove to be more than a match for Godzilla and Anguirus; to make matters worse, Godzilla is badly injured by the Nebulans when the Godzilla Tower fires an extremely powerful laser weapon at Godzilla, and is rapidly overpowered by Gigan's assortment of bladed weapons. However, Gengo and his friends come to the aid of Godzilla and Anguirus when they destroy Godzilla Tower with TNT supplied by the JSDF, killing the Nebulans and leaving Ghidorah and Gigan without instruction.
Though the extraterrestrial monsters manage to regain their composure and briefly resume the fight, Godzilla and Anguirus now have the upper hand, and manage to drive both Ghidorah and Gigan into a full retreat. With the invasion defeated, Godzilla and Anguirus begin the return trip to Monster Island, much to the cheers of the humans who helped them fend off their opponents.

title: Josie and the Pussycats
tagline: They were three small time girls, with big time dreams. Now, fate is giving the Pussycats, the chance of a lifetime.
overview: Josie, Melody and Val are three small-town girl musicians determined to take their rock band out of their garage and straight to the top, while remaining true to their look, style and sound. They get a record deal which brings fame and fortune but soon realize they are pawns of two people who want to control the youth of America. They must clear their names, even if it means losing fame and fortune.
plot:
Successful boy band DuJour, signed to the pop music record label MegaRecords, are set to perform on a world tour. While on an airplane, they confront MegaRecords label executive Wyatt Frame to express concern about a strange backing track they have discovered on their single "DuJour Around the World". The band members subsequently get into a fight, and Wyatt parachutes out of the jet, leaving it to descend and presumably kill the band.
Landing outside the town of Riverdale, Wyatt searches for a replacement band. He plays DuJour's most recent track at a music store, causing the young crowd to respond to the subliminal messaging, and causes the kidnapping of a "free-thinking" individual who dislikes the music. Wyatt eventually encounters the Pussycats: lead vocalist and guitarist Josie McCoy, drummer Melody Valentine, and bassist and backup vocalist Valerie Brown. The struggling local pop-punk band and their manager, Alexander Cabot, accept Wyatt's offer of a major record deal despite its seeming implausibility, and they fly to New York City. Wyatt renames the band "Josie and the Pussycats", arguing that the public needs to identify with the lead singer.
Meanwhile, MegaRecords CEO Fiona, in an underground meeting with world government representatives, details how the United States government has conspired with the music industry to hide subliminal messages in pop music to indoctrinate teenagers into buying trendy consumer products, thus helping to build a robust economy from the money the teenagers earn from minimum wage jobs such as babysitting. Musicians who discover the hidden messages are made to disappear via staged plane crashes, drug overdoses, controversial scandals, and similar disasters.
Josie and the Pussycats' first single "Pretend to Be Nice" is released and, due to subliminal messaging, instantly becomes successful, soon topping the charts. However, Valerie increasingly resents the attention the label gives Josie rather than the band as a whole, while Melody's behavioral perception makes her suspicious of Fiona and Wyatt. Fiona orders Wyatt to kill Valerie and Melody before they uncover the conspiracy. The Pussycats are supposedly sent to an appearance on MTV's TRL where Carson Daly and his impersonator attempt to kill them with baseball bats, though the girls survive due to their attackers' incompetence.
Rather than allow her to attend a gig by her friend Alan M., claiming it was cancelled, Wyatt instead gives Josie a copy of the group's latest single "You Don't See Me", which contains a subliminal message track designed to brainwash her into desiring a solo career. After arguing with her bandmates to the point where they leave, Josie realizes that the single caused the fight. Josie searches for Valerie and Melody, and with the help of Alexander and his sister, Alexandra, she confirms her suspicions when she uses a mixing board to isolate the subliminal track. However, Fiona and her cronies catch Josie unaware.

overview: When her nation is invaded, a young princess is taken into the Princess Protection Program. She is relocated to Louisiana, where she stays with a covert agent and his tomboyish daughter, and must learn how to behave like an ordinary teenager.
plot:
Princess Protection Program is a 2009 American comedy television film produced as a Disney Channel Original Movie, directed by Allison Liddi-Brown and written by Annie DeYoung from a story by DeYoung and David Morgasen. Demi Lovato stars as Princess Rosalinda and Selena Gomez as Carter Mason, with Tom Verica as her father, Nicholas Braun and Molly Hagan. It premiered on Disney Channel on 26 June 2009 and was released on DVD shortly afterwards.

Princess Rosalinda María Montoya Fioré is about to be crowned queen of the small nation of Costa Luna when her coronation rehearsal is interrupted by General Magnus Kane, the dictator of neighboring Costa Estrella, whose forces storm the palace in an attempt to seize the country. Major Joe Mason, an agent of the Princess Protection Program, a secret organization funded by royal families to protect endangered princesses, rescues Rosalinda by helicopter, but Kane's men capture her widowed mother, Queen Sofía.

While the program works to remove Kane from power and free her kingdom, Rosalinda is hidden at Joe's home in rural Louisiana, where she meets his daughter, Carter, an insecure tomboy who works at the family bait shop and dreams of going to the homecoming dance with her crush, Donny, unaware that her classmate Ed likes her. Rosalinda poses as Rosie Gonzalez, Carter's cousin from Iowa. Carter is hostile at first, but warms to her after learning her story, and the two become close friends. Carter teaches Rosie to act like an ordinary American teenager, while Rosie shows Carter how to carry herself with the confidence of a princess. Rosie becomes popular at school and is nominated for homecoming queen, angering a snobbish classmate, Chelsea. Meanwhile, Kane is determined to find the princess and secure his hold on Costa Luna, and when his agents track her down, Carter devises a plan to protect her friend, leading to a confrontation at the homecoming dance.

The film drew more than eight million viewers on its premiere and won the Teen Choice Award for Choice Summer Movie. Laura Fries of Variety described it as light as a summer breeze on the Louisiana bayou, praising its message about self-esteem and predicting it would be a hit with the channel's audience.

plot:
One Piece: The Movie is a 2000 Japanese animated adventure film based on the popular manga and anime series of the same name, created by Eiichiro Oda. The movie was produced by Toei Animation and directed by Shūta Kawamori.

The story begins with Monkey D. Luffy, a young boy who has eaten the Gum-Gum Fruit, which gives him the ability to stretch and manipulate his body like rubber. Luffy's dream is to become the Pirate King, inspired by his idol, Shanks. He sets out on a journey to find the legendary treasure known as "One Piece," said to be hidden by the late pirate Gol D. Roger.

Luffy meets Roronoa Zoro, a skilled swordsman and member of the Straw Hat Pirates, who joins him on his quest. They are soon joined by Usopp, Sanji, Tony Tony Chopper, Nico Robin, Franky, Brook, and Nami, each with their unique abilities and personalities.

The movie follows Luffy and his crew as they face various challenges and enemies, including the World Government's agents, who seek to capture Luffy and use him for their own purposes. Along the way, they also encounter other pirates, including Arlong, a powerful fish-man pirate who serves as the main antagonist of the film.

As the story unfolds, Luffy and his crew discover that Arlong is actually a former member of the World Government's elite military unit, known as the "Baroque Works." The group learns that Arlong has been using his powers to terrorize the people of Water 7, where they plan to settle down for a while.

The final confrontation between Luffy and Arlong takes place in the city of Water 7. Luffy uses his rubber powers to fight against Arlong's powerful attacks, but ultimately, it is Chopper who comes up with a plan to defeat him. Using his medical knowledge, Chopper creates an antidote that neutralizes Arlong's powers, allowing Luffy to land the final blow.

In the end, Luffy and his crew successfully defeat Arlong and save the people of Water 7. The movie concludes with Luffy and his friends continuing their journey to find One Piece, while also setting the stage for future adventures in the series.

Overall, One Piece: The Movie is a fun and action-packed adventure that showcases the characters' personalities and abilities. While it may not be as complex or nuanced as some of the later films in the series, it remains an enjoyable entry point for new fans and a nostalgic trip for longtime enthusiasts.

plot:
The Dukes of Hazzard: The Beginning is a 2007 American buddy comedy made for television, directed by Robert Berlinger and produced under Warner Bros.' Warner Premiere label on a budget of about $5 million. A standalone prequel to the 2005 feature The Dukes of Hazzard, it was the fourth and last Dukes of Hazzard film. An edited cut premiered on ABC Family on March 4, 2007, and R-rated and unrated versions reached DVD later that month.

In rural Georgia, teenage cousins Bo Duke, arrested for reckless driving in a neighboring county, and Luke Duke, caught setting off illegal fireworks, are paroled to their Uncle Jesse in Hazzard County and sentenced to a summer of farm labor. Jesse secretly makes the county's finest moonshine and pays regular bribes to the corrupt commissioner, Boss Hogg. When the boys accidentally let Hogg's prized pig escape and it is hurt, Hogg demands a large sum within two weeks or he will seize the farm. To earn the money through moonshine runs, Bo and Luke need a fast car. With help from their shy cousin Daisy and the mechanic Cooter Davenport, who supplies an engine, they pull an abandoned 1969 Dodge Charger out of a swimming hole and rebuild it as the General Lee.

The deliveries succeed until Hogg declares Hazzard a dry county, offers a reward for exposing moonshiners and has Jesse arrested. Daisy, who has taken a job at the Boar's Nest after a dramatic makeover, discovers that the bartender she has fallen for, Hughie, is Hogg's nephew and was spying on the family. The Dukes learn that Hogg wants to ban alcohol across Georgia so he can sell his own liquor illegally. They kidnap him in the General Lee and, threatening to leap a ravine, force a confession that Daisy arranges to have broadcast on the radio. They claim the reward to save the farm, Jesse and the other moonshiners are freed, and the cousins drive off toward new adventures.

Jonathan Bennett plays Bo, Randy Wayne plays Luke and April Scott plays Daisy, with Christopher McDonald as Boss Hogg and Harland Williams as Sheriff Rosco P. Coltrane. Willie Nelson, as Jesse, was the only actor returning from the 2005 film. Reviews were generally negative, and the few critics counted by Rotten Tomatoes gave it a 20% approval rating.

Thea is about to be dismissed by her ill-tempered boss, the publisher Jerry, when she remembers from an episode of Law & Order that it is illegal to fire a woman because she is pregnant, and claims that she is expecting a baby. Soon Jerry is called away, and his younger brother Nick, an accountant, takes over the running of the company.

Hoping to sign the popular author Suzie Cavandish, who has written a book about pregnancy, Nick brings Thea along to the meeting, and Thea's enthusiasm persuades the writer to publish with them. Nick launches a new parenting division and promotes Thea to editor, complete with a raise. Thea's younger sister Emma is shocked to discover her apparent pregnancy, and Thea must explain the deception. As Thea grows closer to Nick and their relationship becomes romantic, she finds herself caught up in her own lie, attending prenatal classes and pregnancy events and becoming an unlikely spokeswoman for expectant mothers, all while knowing that the truth will eventually come out and could cost her both her job and the man she loves.

Labor Pains received negative reviews from critics, who considered the premise thin and the humor flat, and its move from cinemas to cable television was widely seen as a sign of Lohan's declining career at the time. title: In the Loop
tagline: The fate of the world is on the line.
overview: The US President and the UK Prime Minister are planning on launching a war in the Middle East, but—behind the scenes—government officials and advisers are either promoting the war or are trying to prevent it.
plot:
At a time when the United Kingdom and the United States are contemplating military intervention in the Middle East, the UK Minister for International Development, Simon Foster, offhandedly states during an interview on BBC Radio 4's Today programme that war in the region is "unforeseeable". The Prime Minister's Director of Communications, Malcolm Tucker, castigates Simon and warns him to toe the line. Toby Wright, Simon's new special adviser, is dating Suzy, who works in the Foreign Office, and he takes the credit when she gets Simon an invite to that day's Foreign Office–State Department meeting.
The US Assistant Secretary of State for Diplomacy, Karen Clark, opposes military intervention, and, at the meeting, she flags a report—titled "Post-War Planning: Parameters, Implications, and Possibilities" (PWPPIP)—by her aide Liza Weld about the pros and cons of intervention, which features many more cons than pros and contains caveats for most of the pros. Ambushed by reporters afterward, Simon rambles that the government must be prepared to "climb the mountain of conflict", and is again chastised by Malcolm, though the Prime Minister decides to send Simon to the US to gather information about problems that might arise for the UK in the event of a war.
Back in Washington, DC, hawkish US Assistant Secretary of State for Policy Linton Barwick is concerned that his secret war committee was mentioned during the Foreign Office meeting; Karen and Liza deduce that it is named the Future Planning Committee. Karen teams up with Lieutenant General George Miller, who opposes the war because he believes the US has insufficient military personnel available, and invites Simon to the upcoming meeting of the Future Planning Committee to "internationalize the dissent". Toby thoughtlessly leaks the true nature of the committee to a friend at CNN, and then meets up with Liza, whom he knows from university, at a bar, and they end up sleeping together.
Owing to Toby's leak, the Future Planning Committee meeting is swamped by reporters. Both Karen and Linton turn to Simon to back their respective causes, but he struggles to say anything meaningful in support of either. Malcolm arrives and confronts Linton about sending him to a diversionary briefing at the White House, and Linton asks him to supply the US with British intelligence that will support military intervention.
Back in Simon's Northampton constituency, a resident named Paul Michaelson urges him to do something about his constituency office wall, which is in danger of collapsing into Paul's mother's garden. When Paul feels ignored, he contacts the media, and there is growing criticism over Simon's inaction. Suzy finds out about Toby's one-night stand with Liza and breaks up with him, but as he is moving out of their apartment, he leaves her a copy of PWPPIP, asking her to leak it; she chastises him for not doing it himself.

title: I Love You, Beth Cooper
tagline: Popularity is nice. Popular girls are not.
overview: A valedictorian's declaration of love for a high-school cheerleader launches a night of revelry, reflection and romance for a group of graduating seniors.
plot:
I Love You, Beth Cooper is a 2009 American coming-of-age comedy film directed by Ken Kwapis and written by Michael Borkow. The movie stars Nathan Lee Graham, Lizzy Caplan, and Hayden Christensen.

The story revolves around Jules (Nathan Lee Graham), a high school senior who has always been the class clown and ladies' man. However, after being dumped by his girlfriend, Beth Cooper (Lizzy Caplan), on their graduation day, Jules is left feeling empty and uncertain about his future.

Beth, the popular and beautiful cheerleader, had been Jules' on-again, off-again girlfriend for years. Despite her initial reluctance to commit, she had always seemed to be the one person who truly understood Jules. However, on their graduation day, Beth suddenly breaks up with him, leaving Jules heartbroken.

As Jules navigates his post-high school life, he begins to realize that he has been living in a state of emotional numbness, using humor and superficial relationships to avoid dealing with his true feelings. He starts to question the choices he's made and the people he's surrounded himself with.

Meanwhile, Beth is struggling to find her place in the world after high school. She feels pressure from her parents to attend college and pursue a career, but she's not sure what she wants to do with her life.

As Jules and Beth reconnect at their high school reunion, they begin to re-examine their past relationship and confront the reasons why it ended. Through a series of awkward and humorous encounters, they start to understand each other better and develop feelings for each other again.

However, just as things are starting to look up, Jules receives an unexpected phone call from his estranged father, who has been absent from his life for years. The call forces Jules to confront the reality of his family dynamics and the choices he's made about his own future.

In the end, Jules comes to a realization that he needs to take control of his life and make amends with his past. He musters up the courage to have an honest conversation with Beth and himself, leading to a heartwarming and humorous conclusion.

Throughout the movie, the title "I Love You, Beth Cooper" serves as a metaphor for Jules' journey of self-discovery and growth. The phrase is often used in a sarcastic tone by Jules, but ultimately becomes a genuine expression of his love and appreciation for Beth and himself.

Overall, I Love You, Beth Cooper is a charming and relatable coming-of-age story that explores themes of identity, relationships, and finding one's true self.

title: The Stepfather
tagline: Daddy's home
overview: Michael Harding returns home from military school to find his mother happily in love and living with her new boyfriend, David. As the two men get to know each other, Michael becomes more and more suspicious of the man who is always there with a helpful hand. Is he really the man of her dreams or could David be hiding a dark side?
plot:
The Stepfather is a 2009 American psychological horror film directed by Nelson McCormick. It remakes the 1987 film of the same name, which was loosely inspired by the crimes of mass murderer John List, and is the fourth film in the series. Dylan Walsh plays the title character, with Sela Ward as Susan Harding, Penn Badgley as her son Michael, Amber Heard as Michael's girlfriend Kelly and Jon Tenney as Susan's ex-husband Jay.

In a Utah suburb, a man named Grady Edwards shaves his beard, dyes his hair and removes colored contact lenses before leaving behind the bodies of his wife and three children. Police link the murders to a similar massacre in New Jersey. In Oregon, recently divorced mother Susan Harding meets a charming widower who calls himself David Harris, and they rush into an engagement. Her eldest son, Michael, returns from military school and becomes suspicious, especially when David gets the name of his late daughter wrong and keeps the basement cabinets locked.

David kills anyone who threatens his new identity. A neighbor who saw a TV profile of a serial killer resembling him is pushed down her basement stairs and smothered. He quits his job with Susan's sister Jackie rather than show identification. When Jay questions his past, David kills him with a vase and a plastic bag and then uses Jay's phone to text Michael that everything checks out. When Jackie plans to hire an investigator, he drowns her in her pool. Ignoring Kelly's attempts to distract him with college plans, Michael breaks into the basement and finds his father's body in a freezer before David knocks Kelly out and locks him in. David's identity begins to crack in front of Susan, and he asks, "Who am I here?" She flees to the bathroom and stabs him in the neck with a shard of mirror. He gets up again and chases the family into the attic. He and Michael fall from the roof. Michael wakes from a month-long coma to learn that David escaped. In the final scene, under the new name Chris Ames, he meets a woman shopping with her two sons at a hardware store.

Terry O'Quinn, star of the original, reportedly declined a cameo. Filming ended in April 2008, and Sony Pictures released the film on October 16, 2009. It opened fifth with $11.6 million and grossed $31.2 million against a $20 million budget. Critics were largely negative, and Rotten Tomatoes called it a tepid remake that lacks the original's tension and satire, though the Los Angeles Times praised its craft and performances.

title: The Goods: Live Hard, Sell Hard
