title: Sin Nombre
tagline: The greatest sin of all is risking nothing.
overview: Sayra, a Honduran teen, hungers for a better life. Her chance for one comes when she is reunited with her long-estranged father, who intends to emigrate to Mexico and then enter the United States. Sayra's life collides with a pair of Mexican gangmembers who have boarded the same American-bound train.
plot:
Sin Nombre is a 2009 American drama film directed by Cary Joji Fukunaga, written by Fukunaga and Eric Warren Singer, and starring Diego Luna, Jeremy Renner, and Woody Harrelson.

The movie follows the story of Elmer Escalante (Diego Luna), a young Guatemalan migrant who is traveling north through Mexico with his cousin, Valentina (Paola Mendoza). They are part of a large group of migrants attempting to reach the United States in search of a better life. The group faces numerous challenges and dangers along the way, including corrupt border patrol agents, ruthless coyotes (human smugglers), and treacherous terrain.

As Elmer navigates this perilous journey, he meets Alejandro (Jeremy Renner), a seasoned migrant who has been traveling for years. Alejandro is initially portrayed as a tough, no-nonsense individual who is driven by a desire to reach the United States and start anew. However, as the story progresses, it becomes clear that Alejandro's motivations are more complex, and he is haunted by his past.

Throughout the film, Elmer forms a bond with Alejandro, who becomes a sort of mentor to him. As they face various challenges together, Elmer learns valuable lessons about resilience, courage, and the importance of human connection in the face of adversity.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Alejandro's past is marked by tragedy and loss. He has been searching for his sister, who disappeared during a previous migration attempt. This personal quest drives much of Alejandro's actions throughout the film, as he hopes to find her and bring closure to his own emotional scars.

The film's climax features a dramatic confrontation between Elmer and Alejandro, as they are forced to make a difficult decision about their future. Ultimately, Elmer decides to continue on his journey, while Alejandro chooses to turn back and return to Mexico.

The movie ends with Elmer standing alone at the border, looking out at the vast expanse of the United States. He is filled with a mix of emotions - hope, fear, and uncertainty about what lies ahead. The camera lingers on his face, capturing the complexity and vulnerability of this young migrant's journey.

Throughout Sin Nombre, Fukunaga explores themes of migration, identity, and the human cost of globalization. The film offers a powerful and unflinching portrayal of the challenges faced by migrants, as well as the resilience and determination that defines them.

title: Orphan
tagline: There's something wrong with Esther.
overview: After losing their baby, a married couple adopt 9-year old Esther, who may not be as innocent as she seems.
plot:
Orphan is a 2009 American psychological horror-thriller film directed by Jaume Collet-Serra and written by Alex Mace. The movie stars Vera Farmiga, Peter Sarsgaard, and Isabelle Fuhrman.

The story begins with the adoption of Esther (Isabelle Fuhrman), an orphaned girl from Eastern Europe, by the Duncan family - Kate (Vera Farmiga) and John (Peter Sarsgaard) along with their six-year-old son Daniel. The Duncans are struggling to cope with the loss of their previous child, who died in a car accident.

Initially, Esther seems like an ideal addition to the family, but strange occurrences start to happen. She is extremely intelligent, obedient, and eerily mature for her age. As time passes, Kate begins to notice that Esther's behavior is not normal, and she starts to suspect that something is amiss.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Esther has a dark secret: she was born with a rare genetic disorder called "progeria," which causes accelerated aging. However, this condition also makes her extremely intelligent and manipulative. Esther's true intentions are slowly revealed as she begins to manipulate the Duncans, using her intelligence and charm to get what she wants.

As Kate becomes more suspicious of Esther, she starts to investigate her past, only to discover that Esther was actually a 12-year-old girl who had been abandoned by her parents in Eastern Europe. The truth about Esther's age is revealed when Daniel discovers an old photograph of Esther as a young girl, which shows her with a younger brother.

The climax of the movie takes place at a family dinner, where Kate confronts Esther about her true identity and intentions. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Esther had been planning to kill Daniel all along, using her intelligence and manipulation to make him believe she was his sister. The movie ends with Kate being killed by Esther, who then escapes.

The ending scene shows an elderly woman, believed to be Esther's mother, visiting the Duncans' home. She is revealed to be a 60-year-old woman, not the young girl Esther claimed to be. This twist suggests that Esther had been lying about her age and identity from the beginning, and that she had been manipulating the Duncans all along.

Overall, Orphan is a tense and suspenseful thriller that explores themes of identity, manipulation, and the dangers of underestimating others. The movie features strong performances from its cast, particularly Vera Farmiga and Isabelle Fuhrman, who bring depth and complexity to their characters.

title: Barbershop 2: Back in Business
tagline: Let your hair down
overview: The continuing adventures of the barbers at Calvin's Barbershop. Gina, a stylist at the beauty shop next door, is now trying to cut in on his business. Calvin is again struggling to keep his father's shop and traditions alive--this time against urban developers looking to replace mom & pop establishments with name-brand chains. The world changes, but some things never go out of style--from current events and politics to relationships and love, you can still say anything you want at the barbershop.
plot:
Since the events of the previous film, Calvin Palmer Jr. has finally settled comfortably into his role as the owner of the Chicago South Side barbershop founded by his late grandfather. The shop's latest threat comes from overzealous developer Quentin Leroux, who opens a rival barbershop across the street called Nappy Cutz.
While Calvin attempts to figure out how to deal with the coming threat of direct competition from Quentin's flashy establishment, his barbers are having their own problems. Isaac, the lone white barber, is now the star of the shop, and begins to feel that he deserves star treatment, feeling neglected by Calvin and the other barbers. Terri is finding success in managing her anger but she has trouble dealing with the growing mutual attraction between Ricky (Michael Ealy) and herself. Dinka is still interested in Terri but is distraught when he finds out that she loves Ricky instead. Jimmy has quit the shop to work for local alderman Lalowe Brown; his replacement, Calvin's cousin Kenard, is fresh out of barber school and horribly inept at cutting hair. Meanwhile, the barbershop and other businesses like it are under threat from gentrification, and Calvin is offered a substantial bribe from both Leroux and Alderman Brown in exchange for his support of the city council's gentrification legislation.
A subplot involves Eddie recalling his time as a young man in the late 1960s, when he first started working at the shop with Calvin's father, including the riots following the assassination of Martin Luther King Jr. Also, Eddie remembers his long-lost love, Loretta (Garcelle Beauvais-Nilon). Eddie and Calvin begin bonding. The film also introduces Calvin's good friend and ex-lover, Gina Norris, who works at the beauty shop next door. The girls at the beauty shop have similar conversations and experiences as the barbers and Gina has a bitter rivalry with Eddie.
After attempting to change his own barbershop's style and decor to match those of his rival, Calvin decides to refuse the bribe money and speak out against the neighborhood's gentrification at the local city council meeting. Though Calvin gives a passionate speech about the legislation helping the region to earn money at the cost of its soul and the community, the council still unanimously votes to approve the legislation and move forward with the project. Despite a mutual attraction, Terri and Ricky agree to remain friends, but not before sharing one last kiss. Dinka still loses out on Terri, but finds love with a stylist at Gina's beauty shop. Though the gentrification project is approved, the community remains loyal to Calvin's barbershop.

title: All the Pretty Horses
tagline: Some passions can never be tamed.
overview: The year is 1949. A young Texan named John Grady finds himself without a home after his mother sells the ranch where he has spent his entire life. Lured south of the border by the romance of cowboy life and the promise of a fresh start, Cole and his pal embark on an adventure that will test their resilience, define their maturity, and change their lives forever.
plot:
All the Pretty Horses is a 2000 American Western produced and directed by Billy Bob Thornton, adapted from Cormac McCarthy's 1992 novel of the same name, the first book of his Border Trilogy. Matt Damon leads a cast that includes Henry Thomas, Lucas Black, Penélope Cruz, Rubén Blades, Robert Patrick, Bruce Dern and Sam Shepard. Miramax Films released it in the United States on December 25, 2000, with Columbia Pictures distributing in other territories.

The story is set in 1949. Young Texas cowboy John Grady Cole finds himself without a home after his family's ranch is sold following his grandfather's death. Unwilling to give up the only way of life he knows, he persuades his best friend Lacey Rawlins to leave San Angelo with him and ride on horseback roughly 150 miles south across the border to look for work in Mexico. Along the trail they fall in with Jimmy Blevins, a strange, headstrong teenager riding a fine horse, but after he loses the animal in a storm and causes trouble trying to recover it, the pair part ways with him.

Cole and Rawlins find work as hands on a large hacienda, where the owner, Don Héctor, is impressed by their skill with horses. Cole falls in love with Alejandra Villarreal, the rancher's beautiful daughter, but the romance is firmly opposed by her aunt, Dueña Alfonsa, who guards the family's honor. After Alejandra is sent away, Cole and Rawlins are arrested by Mexican police and reunited with Blevins, who has been accused of horse theft and murder. The boy is executed by a corrupt police captain, and the two friends are thrown into a brutal Mexican prison as accomplices, where they must fight to stay alive. Their eventual release comes at a heavy price, and Cole is left to decide what he owes to Alejandra, to his friend and to the dead Blevins.

The production became known for a protracted dispute between Thornton and the studio over its length. Thornton's original cut ran close to four hours and was considerably shortened for theatrical release, and Daniel Lanois's score was largely replaced. The finished film was poorly received. On Rotten Tomatoes it holds a 32% approval rating from 100 reviews, with critics describing it as a weak adaptation of the novel and dramatically inert, and it grossed only about $18.1 million worldwide against a much larger budget.

title: Merlin and the Book of Beasts
original_title: Merlin and the Book of Beasts
overview: In the twenty years since the fall of Camelot, Merlin has become a recluse known as "the wild man of the woods." He is now summoned by a charge of young knights as they quest to destroy an evil wizard who rules the land from a throne of a "New Camelot."
plot:
Merlin and the Book of Beasts is a 2009 Canadian fantasy television film directed by Warren P. Sonoda from a screenplay by Brook Durham, made by Front Street Pictures for Syfy. Drawing loosely on Arthurian legend, it stars James Callis as the wizard Merlin and Laura Harris as Avlynn, the daughter of King Arthur and Guinevere. The film was shot in Langley and Maple Ridge, British Columbia, and premiered on American television on 30 May 2009.

Twenty years after the death of Arthur and the fall of Camelot, the castle is ruled by the sorcerer Arkadian, who draws his power from the Book of Beasts, a magical tome that unleashes monstrous creatures. Avlynn sets out with the last of the knights, among them Sir Galahad, his son Lysanor and Tristan, to find Merlin, Arthur's old counsellor, now living as a recluse in an enchanted forest and known as the wild man of the woods. Merlin at first refuses to help, but eventually joins the quest to retake Camelot, which also requires Avlynn to find Excalibur. Arkadian is revealed to be Mordred, Arthur's son by Morgan le Fay and thus Avlynn's half-brother.

Along the way Merlin is struck down, and the company carries him to a legendary healing well, only to find it dry. Galahad urges them to leave him behind, but Avlynn refuses and draws water from the well with her own blood, reviving the wizard, who then dispatches a pack of Medusa-like creatures sent by Arkadian. At the Lake of Destiny Avlynn recovers her father's sword, before the group is captured by giant birds under the sorcerer's control. Arkadian tries to seduce Avlynn by taking on the appearance of Lysanor, with whom she is in love. In the final battle Merlin strips Arkadian of his magic and binds his spirit within Camelot, while Avlynn uses Excalibur to pin the Book of Beasts to a rock, saving Merlin from being consumed by it.

The supporting cast includes Jim Thorburn as Arkadian, Jesse Moss as Lysanor, Donald Adams as Galahad and Patrick Sabongui as Tristan, with Monique Ganderton, Maja Aro, Megan Vincent and Daniel Cudmore. Produced with Starz and Magical Trail Productions, the film was later released on DVD in several countries, including Japan and Germany. Reception was poor, with an audience score of only about 15 percent on Rotten Tomatoes from more than 250 ratings.

title: Mickey, Donald, Goofy: The Three Musketeers
original_title: Mickey, Donald, Goofy: The Three Musketeers
tagline: All for fun and fun for all
overview: In Disney's take on the Alexander Dumas tale, Mickey Mouse, Donald Duck and Goofy want nothing more than to perform brave deeds on behalf of their queen (Minnie Mouse), but they're stymied by the head Musketeer, Pete. Pete secretly wants to get rid of the queen, so he appoints Mickey and his bumbling friends as guardians to Minnie, thinking such a maneuver will ensure his scheme's success. The score features songs based on familiar classical melodies.
plot:
Mickey, Donald, Goofy: The Three Musketeers is an American animated musical adventure of 2004 directed by Donovan Cook and produced by Walt Disney Pictures with the Australian unit of Disneytoon Studios. Loosely drawn from Alexandre Dumas's novel, it was the first feature-length film to star the three friends together. Wayne Allwine voices Mickey Mouse, Tony Anselmo Donald Duck and Bill Farmer both Goofy and Pluto, with Russi Taylor as Minnie, Tress MacNeille as Daisy, Jim Cummings as Pete, April Winchell as Clarabelle Cow and Rob Paulsen as the narrating Troubadour.

The Troubadour, a music-loving French tortoise, tells the tale from his comic book. In 17th-century France, the street urchins Mickey, Donald, Goofy and Pluto are rescued from the bullying Beagle Boys by royal musketeers, who give Mickey a hat and inspire the friends to become musketeers themselves. Years later they are merely janitors at musketeer headquarters, run by Captain Pete, who secretly plans to depose Princess Minnie and crown himself king. After the Beagle Boys, in Pete's pay, nearly assassinate her, Minnie demands musketeer bodyguards, and Pete appoints the three janitors, assuming they will be easy to dispose of.

On a carriage ride the Beagle Boys kidnap Minnie and her lady-in-waiting Daisy. Mickey and Goofy track them to a tower and defeat them while a frightened Donald hangs back, and Mickey and Minnie begin a romance. Pete then targets the heroes one by one: his lieutenant Clarabelle lures Goofy away and tries to drown him in the Seine, only to fall in love with him, while Mickey, warned by Donald of Pete's treachery, is locked in a flooding dungeon at Mont Saint-Michel. Scolded by the Troubadour for his cowardice, Donald joins Goofy and Pluto to free Mickey. At the opera, where a disguised Beagle Boy posing as Minnie proclaims Pete king, the musketeers battle the villains on stage and rescue the princess and Daisy, who declare their love for Mickey and Donald. Minnie then makes the three friends royal musketeers at last.

The songs set new comic lyrics to classical pieces and include a cover of "Three Is a Magic Number". After a limited screening at the El Capitan Theatre, the film was released on DVD and VHS on 17 August 2004, the first Disney DVD with the FastPlay feature. Reviews were mixed, praising the music and action, and it scored 42% on Rotten Tomatoes.

plot:
Mickey's Magical Christmas: Snowed In At The House Of Mouse is a direct-to-video animated film produced by Disney Television Animation, released in 2001. The movie takes place during the holiday season and revolves around Mickey Mouse and his friends at the House of Mouse.

The story begins with Mickey Mouse excitedly preparing for Christmas at the House of Mouse. However, on Christmas Eve, a severe snowstorm hits Toontown, causing the power to go out and trapping the guests inside the restaurant. As the night progresses, the group starts to get restless, and tensions rise as they realize that they won't be able to leave.

As the hours pass, Mickey tries to keep everyone's spirits high by telling Christmas stories and singing holiday songs. However, things take a turn when Pete, who has been trying to ruin Christmas for the gang all along, reveals his true intentions: he plans to steal Santa's bag of presents meant for Toontown.

Determined to stop Pete, Mickey rallies his friends, including Minnie Mouse, Pluto, and Goofy. Together, they devise a plan to outsmart Pete and save Christmas. Along the way, they learn valuable lessons about teamwork, friendship, and the true meaning of the holiday season.

As the night wears on, the group faces various obstacles, including a wild goose chase through the House of Mouse and a confrontation with Pete's accomplices. However, in the end, Mickey and his friends successfully thwart Pete's plans, and Christmas is saved.

The movie concludes with a heartwarming celebration of the holiday season, featuring festive music, decorations, and a special appearance by Santa Claus himself. The film ends on a high note, with Mickey and his friends enjoying a joyful Christmas Eve together, surrounded by the magic of the House of Mouse.

Throughout the movie, the characters' personalities shine through, adding to the humor and charm of the story. From Goofy's goofy antics to Pluto's loyal companionship, each character brings their unique voice to the film, making it a delightful holiday treat for audiences of all ages.

Overall, Mickey's Magical Christmas: Snowed In At The House Of Mouse is a fun, festive, and heartwarming animated film that captures the spirit of the holiday season. With its lovable characters, engaging storyline, and catchy music, this movie is sure to become a classic among Disney fans and families alike.

title: Twitches
tagline: This Halloween, broomsticks are so not happenin'.
overview: Twins separated at birth, Camryn and Alex meet by chance for the first time on their 21st birthday and discover they're witches with the power to save their homeland of Coventry from the evil that threatens it. But when Camryn leaves Alex to face the darkness alone, will Coventry be doomed? Or will the sisters multiply their magic by standing together?
plot:
Twitches is an American fantasy comedy-drama of 2005 made as a Disney Channel Original Movie, directed by Stuart Gillard and written by Melissa Gould and Dan Berendsen, based on the Twitches book series by H. B. Gilmour and Randi Reisfeld. Tia and Tamera Mowry star as Alex Fielding and Camryn Barnes, twin witches separated at birth, with Kristen Wilson as their mother Miranda, Patrick Fabian as their uncle Thantos. It premiered on 14 October 2005.

In the magical realm of Coventry, the royal witch Miranda gives birth to identical twin girls on Halloween night. Named Apolla and Artemis, they wear sun and moon amulets. Their father, the powerful warlock Aron DuBaer, dies after pouring all his magic into protecting them from an evil force called the Darkness. The family friends Karsh and Ileana spirit the babies away to Earth and give them up for adoption. Apolla is raised by a wealthy couple as Camryn Barnes, while Artemis is raised by a single mother as Alex Fielding.

Alex grows up a night owl who writes stories about magical twin sisters without knowing they are true. Camryn, an early riser and passionate artist, unknowingly sketches Miranda and Coventry. On their 21st birthday, Karsh and Ileana steer Alex into the shop where Camryn is trying on clothes. Camryn is thrilled, but when she grabs the fleeing Alex's hand, a burst of energy releases their powers. The guardians reveal the sisters' origins and a prophecy that only they can defeat the Darkness and restore Coventry. Alex, whose stories all end in death, wants no part of it, but Camryn persuades her, and the two practice their magic and grow close.

Miranda, now married to Aron's brother Thantos, senses that her daughters are alive. When the Darkness reaches Alex's apartment, the twins escape to Coventry, but the overwhelmed Camryn returns to Earth for her birthday party. Alex stays and meets Thantos, who warns that Camryn is powerless alone. At the party, Camryn learns from the Darkness itself that Thantos controls it, and she escapes to Coventry as Karsh and Ileana sacrifice themselves to help her. Exposed, Thantos admits murdering Aron for wealth and power, seizes Miranda and rampages through the castle until the twins unite their magic of light and love to destroy him, restoring Coventry and reviving Miranda, Karsh and Ileana. The sisters then celebrate their birthday on Earth with their adoptive families.

Shot in Toronto in 2005, the film was followed by a sequel, Twitches Too, in 2007.

title: Possession
tagline: Inhuman ecstasy fulfilled.
overview: A young woman left her family for an unspecified reason. The husband determines to find out the truth and starts following his wife. At first, he suspects that a man is involved. But gradually, he finds out more and more strange behaviors and bizarre incidents that indicate something more than a possessed love affair.
plot:
Possession is a 1981 psychological horror drama written and directed by Andrzej Żuławski, starring Sam Neill as Mark, a spy, and Isabelle Adjani as his wife Anna, with Heinz Bennent as Anna's lover Heinrich. A French and West German co-production, it is Żuławski's only English-language feature. He wrote the screenplay in the emotional aftermath of his divorce from the actress Małgorzata Braunek and his exile from Poland, and the film was shot in West Berlin in 1980, largely near the Berlin Wall, on a budget of about 2.4 million dollars.

Mark returns home to West Berlin after a mission to find that Anna wants to separate from him and is seeing another man. He gives up their apartment and custody of their young son Bob, but after a long drinking binge he returns to find the boy neglected and decides to care for him himself. Bob's teacher, Helen, turns out to look exactly like Anna, except for her lighter hair and green eyes. Mark confronts Heinrich, an eccentric lover who easily overpowers him, but soon realizes that Anna has been seeing someone, or something, else entirely.

As the couple's encounters turn into scenes of hysterical violence and self-harm, Mark hires a private detective to follow Anna, who has been living in a derelict apartment. There the detective discovers a monstrous tentacled creature that Anna has been nurturing, and she kills him. As more people disappear, Mark is drawn into Anna's madness, killing and covering up crimes to protect her, while the creature gradually transforms, leading to an apocalyptic and deeply ambiguous ending.

The film uses horror to depict the disintegration of a marriage, with themes of jealousy, faith, chance and doubles. Adjani's frenzied performance, including a scene in which Anna suffers a violent miscarriage in the subway, is often singled out as the film's most memorable element. The creature effects were created by Carlo Rambaldi.

Possession premiered at the 34th Cannes Film Festival, where Adjani won the award for Best Actress. It received a lukewarm response on its initial release and was released in a heavily cut version in the United States. In later years the film acquired cult status and has been reappraised as a major work of art-house horror; it holds a Metacritic score of 75.

title: Noroi: The Curse
tagline: Everything is real, everybody died.
overview: A documentary filmmaker explores seemingly unrelated paranormal incidents connected by the legend of an ancient demon called the "kagutaba."
plot:
Noroi: The Curse is a 2005 Japanese horror film directed by Kōji Shiraishi, who co-wrote the screenplay with Naoyuki Yokota, and produced by Takashige Ichise, whose earlier horror productions included Ring and Ju-On: The Grudge. Presented as a finished documentary assembled from pseudo-documentary and found footage, it stars Jin Muraki as paranormal researcher Masafumi Kobayashi, with actress Marika Matsumoto playing a fictionalized version of herself, alongside Rio Kanno, Tomono Kuga and Satoru Jitsunashi, and cameos from the comedy duo Ungirls, Dankan, Ai Iijima and author Hiroshi Aramata. Shiraishi spent about a year on research and interviews, aiming to heighten the fear by grounding the fiction in apparent reality.

The film explains that Kobayashi, known for his books and documentaries on the supernatural, vanished after his house burned down, leaving his wife dead in the ruins, while he was making a documentary called The Curse. That documentary then plays, largely through the footage of his cameraman, Miyajima. Eighteen months earlier, Kobayashi looks into complaints about the sound of crying babies from the home of a woman named Junko Ishii, who moves away soon after, leaving dead pigeons in her yard; days later her neighbor and the neighbor's daughter die in a mysterious car crash. At the same time, a psychic girl named Kana Yano, who appeared on a television variety show, disappears, and an eccentric psychic named Mitsuo Hori claims she was taken by "ectoplasmic worms". After filming at a shrine, Marika Matsumoto collapses on hearing a strange voice and begins weaving yarn and wire into interlocking loops in her sleep, and a camera records a deep voice uttering the word "kagutaba". A local historian tells Kobayashi that Kagutaba is a demon once summoned and then imprisoned by the villagers of Shimokage in Nagano Prefecture, who held an annual ritual to appease it until the village was abandoned to make way for a dam in 1978. As a string of hangings and disappearances follows, Kobayashi uncovers a link between the last ritual and Ishii, drawing him, Marika and Hori ever closer to the demon's influence.

Distributed by Xanadeux, Noroi: The Curse opened in Japan on 20 August 2005 and received generally positive reviews, with critics praising its presentation, performances, atmosphere and pacing. Despite limited distribution outside Japan it developed a following and became legally available in North America through Shudder in 2017.

overview: High school loser (Cannon) pays a cheerleader (Milian) to pose as his girlfriend so he can be considered cool. Remake of 1987's Can't Buy Me Love, starring Patrick Dempsey.

Love Don't Cost a Thing is a 2003 American romantic comedy film directed by David E. Talbert, produced by Alcon Entertainment, and written by David E. Talbert.

The movie follows the story of Derek Matthews (played by Omarion), a high school student who has just transferred to a new school in Los Angeles. Derek is initially hesitant to fit in with his new classmates but eventually befriends two girls: Deena (played by Gabrielle Union) and Nia (played by Brandy Norwood).

Deena, the popular and beautiful cheerleader, catches Derek's eye, and they start dating. However, their relationship is put to the test when Deena starts to develop feelings for her ex-boyfriend, Darius (played by Simon Baker). Meanwhile, Nia, who is initially portrayed as a nerdy and awkward student, reveals her own romantic interests in Derek.

As the story unfolds, Derek finds himself torn between his growing feelings for both Deena and Nia. He struggles to balance his relationships with these two women while navigating high school life. The movie explores themes of love, friendship, and self-discovery as Derek learns valuable lessons about loyalty, trust, and being true to oneself.

Throughout the film, the characters face various challenges, including peer pressure, family expectations, and personal growth. The movie features a mix of humor, drama, and romance, making it an entertaining watch for audiences.

Ultimately, Derek must make a choice between his relationships with Deena and Nia. In the end, he decides to pursue a relationship with Nia, who has been a constant source of support and encouragement throughout his high school journey.

Love Don't Cost a Thing received mixed reviews from critics but was a moderate box office success. The movie's blend of humor, romance, and coming-of-age themes resonated with audiences, particularly young viewers.

title: A Prophet
tagline: Escaping the prison of life.
overview: Sentenced to six years in prison, Malik El Djebena is alone in the world and can neither read nor write. On his arrival at the prison, he seems younger and more brittle than the others detained there. At once he falls under the sway of a group of Corsicans who enforce their rule in the prison. As the 'missions' go by, he toughens himself and wins the confidence of the Corsican group.
plot:
Malik El Djebena, a 19-year-old of Maghrebi descent, is sentenced to six years in prison for attacking police officers. Alone and illiterate upon his arrival, he falls under the sway of Corsican mobsters, led by César Luciani, who enforces a brutal rule.
The prison is divided between two main factions: the Corsicans and the Maghrebis. Malik keeps to himself. When Luciani forces him to be the unwilling assassin of Reyeb, a Maghrebi witness in a trial, Malik gains the protection of the Corsicans despite his North African origin.
Malik serves as a low-level servant to the Corsicans, who treat him with disdain. All the while, he is haunted by visions of the murdered Reyeb.
When most of the Corsicans are transferred or released, Luciani is forced to give Malik more responsibility. Having secretly learned Corsican, Malik acts as Luciani's eyes and ears in the prison. When Malik earns the privilege of day-long furloughs outside the prison, Luciani relies on him to conduct Luciani's criminal business outside.
Ryad, a Maghrebi friend, teaches Malik to read and write, and the two become close. Ryad teaches Malik about his own heritage, introducing him to two other Maghrebis, Tarik and Hassan, and increases his power within the prison.
Malik also becomes involved with a prison drug dealer, Jordi. When Ryad gains an early release due to testicular cancer, the three partners organize a drug-running enterprise to sell hashish. But when Ryad is kidnapped by the drug dealer Latif, Malik tracks down Latif's relative inside the prison. He kidnaps the relative's family and forces Latif's gang to release Ryad.
When Luciani discovers that Malik is using his day-releases for his own personal enterprise, he punishes him by pressing a spoon against his eye. Later on, Malik is sent by César to meet Brahim Lattrache in Marseille, another Maghrebi, who is involved in a deal between Luciani and the Lingherris, an Italian mafia group. Lattrache is bitter toward the Corsicans for the murder of Reyeb and holds Malik at gunpoint. When Malik spots a deer warning sign, he remembers a recent dream of deer running in the road. He tells his kidnappers that they are in danger of hitting wild animals, and they suddenly strike a deer. Lattrache is impressed by Malik, calling him a prophet and agreeing to conduct criminal business with him instead of Luciani, even though Malik admitted that he killed Reyeb.
Luciani believes there is a "mole" in his organization and decides to use Malik to assassinate Jacky Marcaggi, the don of the Corsican mafia, for secretly dealing with the Lingherris. But Malik and Ryad have their own plan for Marcaggi: they kill his bodyguards, kidnap him, and tell him that it was Luciani who ordered the hit before abandoning him in the city.
Malik takes refuge at Ryad's house. The friend's cancer has returned: Ryad's decision to forego more chemotherapy leaves him just six months to live.

title: Batman: Mystery of the Batwoman
tagline: Gotham City's newest hero... or criminal?
overview: As if the Penguin wasn't enough to contend with, a new vigilante has surfaced in Gotham City, and her strong-arm tactics give Batman cause for concern.
plot:
Batman and Robin face a brand-new mystery; a new heroine, Batwoman, has arrived in the city, whose identity is a mystery. While she claims to fight for justice, Batwoman forsakes Batman's code to never take a life. Batman must figure out who she is, while stopping the Penguin and Rupert Thorne from selling illegal weapons to the fictional nation of Kasnia. The two villains employ gangster Carlton Duquesne to provide protection.
Batman, with Robin, sets out to stop Batwoman from making mistakes as she tries to take out the villains and as he encounters numerous twists, setbacks, and apparent false leads in determining her true identity. Bruce Wayne, Batman's alter ego, also becomes romantically involved with Kathy Duquesne, the crime boss' daughter.
In addition to Kathy, Bruce is introduced to two other women who, as his investigation into the Batwoman's true identity continues, seem to fall well into suspicion: Dr. Roxanne "Rocky" Ballantine, a new employee of Wayne Tech, who seemingly but briefly forms a bond with Tim Drake, Robin's alter-ego, and whose technology development Batwoman uses against Penguin; and Detective Harvey Bullock's new partner Sonia Alcana, who seems to know too much about the weapons being smuggled by the Penguin and Carlton Duquesne. With Carlton unable to stop Batwoman's raids on the facilities used to hold the various weapons, the Penguin calls Bane for additional support to ensure that there are no more losses as a result of the Batwoman.
Not long after Bane's arrival in Gotham, it is revealed that there is not one, but three Batwomen, all of whom were the women suspected by Batman. Kathy and Sonia met taking art classes at college, and Sonia and Rocky were roommates; and they all harbor grudges against the Penguin, Thorne, and Carleton Duquesne: the Penguin had framed Rocky's fiancé Kevin, Thorne had burned down a store owned by Sonia's family, and Carlton Duquesne's war with a rival gang got Kathy's mother (his wife) killed. The women took turns to create the illusion of a single Batwoman: Rocky built Batwoman's gadgetry, Kathy financed her efforts, and Sonia created the Batwoman persona as a tribute to Batman, who had saved her life nine years earlier and inspired her to become a police officer.
Kathy plants a bomb in the ship taking the weapons into international waters for the exchange – but not before Bane unmasks her. Kathy and Batman narrowly escape as the bomb goes off, while Carlton forsakes his ties to Thorne and the Penguin to save his daughter's life, and Bane falls into the Gotham River.
Thorne, Penguin, and Duquesne are arrested. Sonia takes the fall for the Batwoman operation, resigns from the GCPD, and decides to leave Gotham. Batman gives Sonia evidence that he discovered which helps clear Rocky's fiancé. Carlton agrees to testify against Thorne and the Penguin in exchange for a lighter sentence. After reconciling with her father, Kathy drives off with Bruce.

title: Cold Prey

overview: When one of them breaks a leg, 5 friends snowboarding in the Norwegian mountains take shelter in a abandoned ski lodge and soon realize they’re not alone.
plot:
In Jotunheimen, a boy with a large birthmark covering the left eye runs frantically through a blizzard, pursued by an unknown entity. Eventually, his pursuer catches up to him and buries him alive in the snow.
Years later, a young group of friends consisting of Jannicke, her boyfriend Eirik, and their friends, Mikal, Ingunn, and Morten Tobias are going on a snowboarding vacation in Jotunheimen. Morten Tobias took a bad fall from skiing and broke his leg. Jannicke sets his leg but they have no cell reception and their car is too far away for medical evacuation. Wandering over a hill, they spot a lodge and decide to seek help there.
Eirik, after discovering that the lodge is deserted, breaks in and opens the door. As Jannicke looks for medical supplies she comes across a box that contains superglue and a single shotgun shell. Jannicke attempts first aid on Morten's broken leg with alcohol and the superglue. Eirik, Mikal and Ingunn explores the abandoned lodge, and discover a generator, which Eirik fixes and restores power to the lodge.
With the lights back on, music playing and plentiful amounts of food and alcohol, the group relaxes in the parlor. Jannicke finds the hotel's guestbook and discovers that the last guest checked in some time in 1975 and there is a message reading "We hope you find your son". Inside the book, there is a picture of a family that includes the boy with a birthmark over his eye.
The group settles in for the night with Mikal and Ingunn running off to a suite, Jannicke and Eirik cuddling under blankets in the parlor, and Morten Tobias alone on the couch. Making out in bed, Ingunn rejected Mikal advances and Mikal leaves to compose himself by the bar. Alone, Ingunn enters the hallway after hearing strange noise and is ambushed by a man wielding a Pickaxe. Her scream for help is drowned out by the music playing and she is stabbed by a pickaxe and dragged away.
The next morning, Eirik leaves the lodge to look for help while Mikal heads to the suite to apologize to Ingunn. Eirik stumbles upon Ingunn's dead body in the snow before being knocked out by an unseen figure. As Mikal receives no replies from Ingunn, he and Jannicke explores the basement and find old important items not usually left behind by travellers.
Jannicke goes to talk to Ingunn only to discover the suite covered in blood. She brings Mikal and Morten Tobias to the bloodied suite, and they realize someone else is in the lodge. They barricade themselves in an empty suite and footsteps are heard in the hall as someone begins to slam against the door, trying to get in. Mikal scouts the lodge after it quiets down and discovers a Massive Mountain Man too tough to deal with before returning to Jannicke.
Mikal tells Jannicke they should run, leaving Morten Tobias but Jannicke refuses. Mikal escapes through the window alone but is caught by a Bear-trap near the shed. Unable to run, he hides in the shed when the Mountain Man approaches.

plot:
Neon Genesis Evangelion: Death and Rebirth is a 1997 Japanese animated film directed by Hideaki Anno, based on the popular anime series Neon Genesis Evangelion. The film serves as a conclusion to the series and provides closure for the characters.

The story begins with Shinji Ikari, the main protagonist, still struggling with his emotional baggage from his past experiences. He is haunted by the guilt of not being able to save his mother, Yui, who died in a catastrophic event known as the "Second Impact." Shinji's relationships with his father, Gendo Ikari, and his friends, Rei Ayanami and Asuka Langley Soryu, are also still unresolved.

The film takes place after the events of the original series, where Shinji has become increasingly isolated and withdrawn. He is visited by a mysterious figure known as "Death," who claims to be an angel from the future. Death reveals that Shinji's existence is tied to the creation of the Evangelion Unit-01, a giant humanoid robot designed to fight against other angels.

As the story unfolds, Shinji discovers that he has the ability to pilot the Evangelion Unit-02, which was created by his father as an alternative to the original unit. However, this new development only serves to further complicate Shinji's emotions and relationships with those around him.

Throughout the film, Anno explores themes of existentialism, psychological trauma, and the nature of humanity. The story is presented in a non-linear fashion, jumping back and forth between different timelines and perspectives.

Ultimately, the film culminates in a confrontation between Shinji and his father, Gendo, who reveals that he has been manipulating events from behind the scenes to bring about the Second Impact. In a final act of desperation, Shinji sacrifices himself to save humanity by destroying the Evangelion Unit-01, which is revealed to be a vessel for the angel Lilith.

In the end, it is implied that Shinji's sacrifice has created a new timeline, one in which he is no longer trapped by his emotional baggage. The film concludes with a sense of hope and renewal, as Shinji's spirit is reborn into a new existence.

Overall, Neon Genesis Evangelion: Death and Rebirth is a thought-provoking and emotionally charged conclusion to the series. It provides closure for the characters while also leaving room for interpretation and speculation about the nature of reality and the human condition.

plot:
Deep in the Valley, released in the United Kingdom as American Hot Babes, is a 2009 American romantic comedy film written and directed by Christian Forte, the son of the 1950s and 1960s teen idol Fabian. It stars Chris Pratt as Lester Watts and Brendan Hines as his best friend Carl, with Scott Caan as the police officer Rod Cannon, Rachel Specter as Bambi Cummings, Christopher McDonald as "Diamond Jim", Denise Richards as Autumn Bliss, Kim Kardashian as Summa Eve, Blanca Soto as Suzi "Diablo" and Tracy Morgan as "Busta Nut".

Lester works in a liquor store, where he cheerfully sells alcohol to minors and spends whatever money he has left on his pornography collection. His best friend since the third grade, Carl, works a corporate job at the family company of his British fiancée, and when he says he wants to quit and find work elsewhere, she angrily tells him that he has no choice but to stay, making it clear that she controls every aspect of their relationship. That night, as the two friends share a beer, a delivery arrives: a vintage porn viewing booth that plays the films of the adult film mogul Diamond Jim. When they step inside, the machine transports them into a world where everyone behaves as if they are in a pornographic movie. They are soon arrested by police officers led by Rod Cannon, but they escape and are hidden from the authorities by Bambi Cummings at her sorority house, Tri-Pi. As the pair evade the police, Carl and Bambi fall in love. Eventually the friends make their way to a pool party at Diamond Jim's mansion, where Carl chooses to be sent home while Lester decides to stay behind, and it is revealed that Lester is in fact Diamond Jim's son. Back in the real world, Carl breaks up with his domineering fiancée, and Bambi is transported to him, reuniting the couple. Meanwhile, Lester takes over his father's adult entertainment empire. In a scene after the closing credits, Rod is revealed to have been transported to the real world, where he has taken over Lester's old job at the liquor store.

The film's soundtrack includes songs by Darius Holbert, Jake Keller and Bang Camaro, whose "Push, Push (Lady Lightning)" is featured.

title: Like Mike
tagline: Think like Mike, Achieve like Mike, Be Like Mike.
overview: Calvin and his friends, who all live in an orphanage, find old shoes with the faded letters MJ connected to a powerline. One stormy night, they go to get the shoes when Calvin and the shoes are struck by lightning. Calvin now has unbelievable basketball powers and has the chance to play for the NBA.
plot:
13-year-old Calvin Cambridge and his two best friends, Murph and Reg Stevens, live in an orphanage in Los Angeles. At night, they all have to sell chocolate for the troublesome orphanage director, Stan Bittleman, at the STAPLES Center, after each home game of the NBA team, the Los Angeles Knights (a parody of the Los Angeles Clippers). Calvin meets the team's coach, who is impressed by Calvin's knowledge of basketball and honesty about the chocolates, and offers Calvin tickets for the next game. Inside a thrift store donation box, Calvin finds a pair of old sneakers with the initials "MJ" written on them; once worn by Michael Jordan. A jealous bully named Ox steals the sneakers and throws them onto an overhead power line. When Calvin tries to retrieve them that night during a rainstorm, he and the sneakers are shocked by a lightning bolt.
The next day, Calvin and his friends attend the game between the Knights and the Minnesota Timberwolves. During a halftime contest, Calvin's ticket number is called and he goes one-on-one with the Knights' star player, Tracy Reynolds. He ends the contest with a slam dunk after bouncing the ball off the backboard. After a long moment of stunned silence, Calvin receives a standing ovation from his friends and the crowd, gets signed to a one-day contract by the Knights, and prepares for his first game with them, but discovers that he is not there to play. When the Knights play the San Antonio Spurs they start losing badly and Coach Wagner decides to let Calvin play in the fourth quarter. Calvin leads a comeback against the Spurs and they win, leading to Calvin getting a season contract. Calvin brings teamwork to the Knights and makes them one of the best teams in the league.
Because Calvin is still a minor, Coach Wagner appoints Tracy to be his roommate and mentor, much to Tracy's displeasure. Late one night, Tracy falls asleep behind the wheel after mistakenly taking sleeping medication, so Calvin is forced to drive the car back to the hotel to keep Tracy from being suspended for violating curfew. While Calvin gets benched for the incident as punishment for "joyriding", Tracy starts warming up to him and the two begin to form a bond.
Bittleman eventually signs a contract with the Knights stating that all of Calvin's money will go to him until Calvin comes of age, or is adopted. When the second option is about to become true, a desperate Bittleman steals Calvin's sneakers and bets $100,000 on the Toronto Raptors to beat the Knights. After the kids convince Ox and his cohorts that Bittleman is selfish, Ox takes the shoes out of Bittleman's safe. The kids head to the arena with Calvin's sneakers. Bittleman escapes and sends goons after Calvin in a failed attempt to retrieve the shoes.
After the third quarter ends with Vince Carter and the Raptors routing the Knights, 80–59, Calvin makes it back to the arena with the shoes.

title: Blood and Bone
tagline: Destroy your enemy
overview: In Los Angeles, an ex-con takes the underground fighting world by storm in his quest to fulfill a promise to a dead friend.
plot:
Blood and Bone is a 2009 American martial arts film directed by Ben Ramsey and written by Michael Andrews. Michael Jai White stars as Isaiah Bone, with Julian Sands, Eamonn Walker, Dante Basco, Nona Gaye, Michelle Belegrin and Bob Sapp in supporting roles. The film also features appearances by a number of well-known fighters, including Matt Mullins, Ernest "The Cat" Miller, Kimbo Slice, Maurice Smith and Gina Carano. It was released direct to DVD on 15 September 2009.

Isaiah Bone is a former marine and martial artist who has just been released from prison. He rents a room in a Los Angeles boarding house owned by Tamara, who is raising her young adopted son Jared. After watching an underground fight won by the local champion Hammerman, Bone makes a deal with a promoter named Pinball, played by Basco, to enter the fighting circuit in exchange for a share of his winnings. He wins his first bout with just two kicks, and night after night defeats every opponent he faces, earning thousands of dollars for himself and Pinball. During this time he bonds with Tamara, Jared and an elderly neighbour named Roberto.

Bone's arrival attracts the attention of James, a ruthless local crime boss played by Walker, and his girlfriend Angela, played by Gaye. Pinball explains that James framed Angela's husband Danny for a triple homicide, sending him to prison, and that she has since fallen into drug addiction. After Bone beats the undefeated Hammerman, James proposes that he face Pretty Boy Price, the champion of an international underground fighting circuit run by the arms dealer Franklin McVeigh, played by Sands. Bone privately reveals to Angela that Danny was his cellmate and friend, and that he was murdered in prison. Angela tells him that she had a son after Danny went to prison but lost custody of him, and Bone sends her to a rehabilitation clinic, promising to reunite her with her child. When James tries to force Bone into the fight by threatening the people he cares about, it becomes clear that Bone has a plan of his own.

The film follows the classic pattern of the underground fighting revenge story, with Bone's quiet sense of honour and loyalty driving the narrative and White's martial arts skills showcased in a series of brutal fight sequences.

Although it was released without a theatrical run, Blood and Bone is remembered chiefly for its fight choreography and for White's physical, charismatic lead performance, which became its main selling point.

title: Bionicle: The Legend Reborn
tagline: A new era must commence
overview: Once the ruler of an entire universe, the Great Spirit Mata Nui finds himself cast out of his own body, his spirit trapped inside the fabled Mask of Life, hurtling through space. After landing on the far-away planet of Bara Magna, the mask creates a new body for Mata Nui, who unwillingly gets caught up in the furious battles of the nearly barren and dangerous planet.
plot:
Bionicle: The Legend Reborn is an animated film that explores several profound themes, primarily centered around identity, self-discovery, and the struggle between light and darkness. 

The story revolves around Gali, a young Toa, who embarks on a perilous journey to reclaim her people's lost city of Metru Nui from the evil Makuta. As she navigates this treacherous world, Gali grapples with her own identity and purpose, questioning whether she is truly destined for greatness or merely a pawn in a larger game.

Throughout her quest, Gali confronts the darkness within herself and the world around her, forcing her to make difficult choices that test her courage, loyalty, and compassion. The film's narrative is replete with symbolism, as Gali's journey serves as a metaphor for the universal human experience of self-discovery and growth.

Ultimately, Bionicle: The Legend Reborn presents a powerful allegory about the importance of embracing one's true nature and finding balance within oneself, while also acknowledging the need to confront and overcome the shadows that threaten to consume us.

title: Minutemen
tagline: It's a short trip from zero... to hero.
overview: When three high-school friends invent a time-machine, they decide to use it to go back in time and prevent other youngsters from making humiliating mistakes.
plot:
Minutemen is a 2008 science fiction Disney Channel Original Movie directed by Lev L. Spiro, with a teleplay by John Killoran from a story by David Diamond and David Weissman. Jason Dolley stars as Virgil Fox, with Luke Benward, Nicholas Braun, Chelsea Staub, Steven R. McQueen and Kara Crane.

On their first day of high school, best friends Virgil, Derek and Stephanie try out different activities. When young genius Charlie disrupts football practice with a homemade rocket-powered vehicle, Virgil tries to help him, and both are publicly humiliated by the jocks. Three years on, Virgil and Charlie are outcasts, while Derek and Stephanie are popular and dating. Charlie designs a time machine, and with Virgil and another outcast, the engineering-minded Zeke, he builds it. On their first trip a street performer ends up keeping a winning lottery ticket meant for them.

The trio then decides to use the machine to undo classmates' humiliations, recruiting Jeannette, who has an unrequited crush on Charlie, to monitor their trips; she provides snowsuits against the freezing temperatures of the time stream. Students hail the anonymous heroes as the "Snowsuit Guys" rather than the "Minutemen" they prefer, while Vice Principal Tolkan sees them as troublemakers. Charlie, who hacked NASA's files to finish the machine, urges restraint, but Virgil uses it to save Stephanie from an injury and reveals his identity to her. At her request he helps Derek undo a loss at the state championship, rekindling those friendships while neglecting Charlie and Zeke, and when Stephanie catches Derek cheating, Virgil, now aware of his own feelings for her, hesitates to undo it. The FBI, which has been tracking them, interrogates the trio, and they split up over Virgil's selfishness. Government scientists tell Charlie that their trips have damaged space-time and created a black hole, and the three reunite to fix it. Sent back to their first day of high school, Virgil considers preventing his friendship with Charlie but learns that Charlie treasures that day and that Derek joined in the humiliation to make the team. The trio escapes the closing black hole, and back in the present nobody remembers their exploits. Virgil confronts Derek and tells Stephanie how he feels.

The film premiered on Disney Channel on January 25, 2008 and with 6.48 million viewers was the most watched program on American cable that week. Spiro received a Directors Guild of America nomination for his work.

title: Shaolin Girl
overview: A Shaolin-trainer young woman returns to Japan to resuscitate her grandfather's defunct martial arts school.
plot:
Shaolin Girl (Shōrin Shōjo) is a 2008 Japanese martial arts sports comedy directed by Katsuyuki Motohiro, best known for the Bayside Shakedown series, from a screenplay by Seishi Togawa and Rika Togawa. Inspired by Stephen Chow's Shaolin Soccer, which it transposes to women's lacrosse, the film stars Ko Shibasaki in her first solo leading role in four years, alongside Toru Nakamura, Kitty Zhang, Takashi Okamura and Yosuke Eguchi. Chow is credited as executive producer, and Tin Kai Man and Lam Chi Chung from Shaolin Soccer appear in similar roles. It was released in Japan on April 26, 2008.

Rin Sakurazawa returns to Japan after 3,000 days of training at a Shaolin martial arts school in China, hoping to spread kung fu at home as her late grandfather wished. She finds his dojo in ruins, and her former teacher Iwai, one of her grandfather's pupils, now runs a Chinese restaurant and urges her to give up her plan. Minmin, who works at the restaurant, persuades Rin to join the women's lacrosse team at Seikan International University, where her astonishing physical ability draws the attention of Tamura, the administrator who manages the team, and Iwai becomes its coach. Left out of the starting line-up for her first match, Rin comes on after a teammate is injured but plays only for herself, and the team falls apart. A game of football with local boys teaches her the meaning of teamwork, and as she wins back her teammates and teaches them the basics of kung fu, both the team and the dojo begin to revive. The university's president, Yuichiro Oba, himself a martial arts master, has been watching her and wants to draw out her hidden power. When his men abduct Minmin, Rin comes to understand Iwai's reluctance to fight and heads to the campus for a final battle to protect her friends.

The film was shot largely around Izunokuni and elsewhere in Shizuoka Prefecture. Its score is by Yugo Kanno, and mihimaru GT performed the theme song "Giri Giri Hero". Reported to have cost over one billion yen, it grossed about 1.51 billion yen in Japan. Critical reception was harsh: critic Kiichiro Yanashita derided it, and the magazine Eiga Hiho named it the worst film of 2008 by a wide margin in its annual poll of critics and writers. It was released in Germany as Kung Fu Girl.

title: Frequently Asked Questions About Time Travel
original_title: Frequently Asked Questions About Time Travel
tagline: Three guys. One pub. Too much time on their hands.
overview: Follows three social outcasts -- two geeks and a cynic -- as they attempt to navigate a time-travel conundrum in the middle of a British pub. Faris plays a girl from the future who sets the adventure in motion.
plot:
Frequently Asked Questions About Time Travel, stylized as FAQ About Time Travel, is a 2009 British science fiction comedy directed by Gareth Carrivick from a screenplay by Jamie Mathieson. Chris O'Dowd, Marc Wootton and Dean Lennox Kelly star as three friends who find themselves caught up in a time-travel conundrum in a pub, with Anna Faris as a mysterious woman from the future and Meredith MacNeill. It was released in the United Kingdom and Ireland on 24 April 2009.

Ray, a science fiction enthusiast who has just been fired from his job as a theme park guide, spends the evening with his friends Pete, a fellow fan, and Toby, a cynical would-be ladies' man. After a trip to the cinema they settle into their local pub, where they compose a sarcastic "Letter to Hollywood" listing their complaints about bad films, written on a page torn from Toby's notebook. Ray then meets Cassie, a woman who claims to be a time traveler sent to repair "time leaks," and who warns him about the Editors, agents from the future who eliminate creative people at the peak of their careers. Ray assumes his friends have set up a prank, while they believe he has invented the encounter.

Soon Pete has a disturbing vision of a massacre in the pub involving a bearded version of himself, and the friends discover a time leak in the men's toilet that sends them half an hour into the past, where they meet earlier versions of themselves. Although Cassie claims to have repaired the leak, the anomalies multiply. The trio find themselves in a post-apocalyptic version of the pub, and Pete briefly vanishes into the leak, returning disheveled and shaken. Trying desperately to avoid paradoxes, they attend a party in the pub themed around their own future selves and meet Millie, who claims to be Cassie's mentor but is in fact an Editor sent to kill them at the moment of their greatest potential. Suspecting that their Letter to Hollywood is the source of their future fame, the friends race to protect it and escape the Editors.

Critical reception was mixed, with a 35 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes. Empire called it quirky and engaging, with a script that keeps viewers on the ride, while the Daily Mirror felt it resembled a stretched-out television pilot but praised it as a nicely made comedy with enough laughs.

title: Thirst
tagline: Lusting after sinful pleasures.
overview: A respected priest volunteers for an experimental procedure that may lead to a cure for a deadly virus. He gets infected and dies, but a blood transfusion of unknown origin brings him back to life. Now, he’s torn between faith and bloodlust, and has a newfound desire for the wife of a childhood friend.
plot:
Thirst (Korean: Bakjwi, literally "Bat") is a 2009 horror film written, produced and directed by Park Chan-wook, based on Émile Zola's 1867 novel Thérèse Raquin. Park had first asked Song Kang-ho to star in a vampire film as early as Joint Security Area, and developed the story with co-writer Chung Seo-kyung. A co-production of South Korea and the United States, it was the first Korean feature made with both Korean and American studio funding and distribution, from CJ Entertainment and Focus Features. It opened in South Korea on 30 April 2009.

Sang-hyun, a Catholic priest who ministers to hospital patients, volunteers for an experiment to find a vaccine against the deadly Emmanuel Virus. He is infected but recovers after a blood transfusion, and his parishioners come to believe he has healing powers. Among the new worshippers is his childhood friend Kang-woo, a sickly man who lives with his overbearing mother, Mrs. Ra, and his wife, Tae-ju. When Sang-hyun relapses, he discovers that he has become a vampire: sunlight burns him and only human blood keeps the disease at bay. Trying not to kill, he steals transfusion packs from the hospital, and he begins a passionate affair with Tae-ju. After she tells him that Kang-woo abuses her, Sang-hyun drowns his friend during a fishing trip.

The couple are haunted by visions of Kang-woo, and Mrs. Ra, drinking heavily, sinks into complete paralysis. When Tae-ju admits that Kang-woo never abused her, Sang-hyun is enraged. Distraught, she asks him to kill her, and he does, but unwilling to be alone forever, he revives her with his own blood. As a vampire, Tae-ju kills without restraint while Sang-hyun feeds only when necessary, and their conflicting ethics lead to violent clashes. When Mrs. Ra reveals their crime to Kang-woo's friends, Tae-ju murders two of them. Sang-hyun destroys his followers' faith in him by pretending to attack a girl, then drives Tae-ju and Mrs. Ra to an open field before dawn. Tae-ju tries to hide, but he thwarts every attempt, and the lovers burn to ash in the rising sun as Mrs. Ra looks on.

Song plays Sang-hyun, with Kim Ok-vin as Tae-ju, Shin Ha-kyun as Kang-woo and Kim Hae-sook as Mrs. Ra. Thirst won the Jury Prize at the 2009 Cannes Film Festival, where it competed for the Palme d'Or, and topped the South Korean box office on its opening weekend. Critics were largely positive, with 81% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and Roger Ebert called Park the most successful horror director working.

title: Scott Pilgrim vs. the World
tagline: Get the hot girl. Defeat her evil exes. Hit love where it hurts.

plot:
Scott Pilgrim vs. the World is a 2010 American action-comedy film directed by Edgar Wright, based on the graphic novel series of the same name by Bryan Lee O'Malley.

The movie follows Scott Pilgrim (played by Michael Cera), a young musician who plays bass guitar in a band called Sex Bob-omb with his friends Stephen Stills (Mark Webber) and Young Neil (Johnny Simmons). Scott is also in a relationship with Knives Chau (Ellen Wong), but he becomes infatuated with Ramona Flowers (Mary Elizabeth Winstead), a mysterious and charismatic girl who has a habit of "dying" and coming back to life.

As Scott tries to win Ramona's heart, he discovers that she is being pursued by seven evil exes, each representing a different aspect of her personality. To defeat these exes and win Ramona's love, Scott must defeat them in a series of musical battles, known as "dance fights."

The first ex, Matthew Patel (Satya Bhabha), is defeated with the help of Ramona's music video. The second ex, Lucas Lee (Chris Evans), is defeated by Scott using his own music video. The third ex, Todd Ingram (Brandon Routh), is a vegan bassist who uses his psychic powers to defeat Scott.

The fourth ex, Roxy Richter (Mae Whitman), is a punk rock singer who is also Ramona's friend. She is defeated with the help of Stephen Stills' music video. The fifth ex, Gideon Graves (Jason Schwartzman), is a successful musician and Ramona's current boyfriend. He is defeated by Scott using his own music video.

The sixth ex, Envy Adams (Brie Larson), is a seductive and manipulative girl who tries to win Scott over. She is defeated with the help of Young Neil's music video. The seventh and final ex, Gideon Graves, is defeated in an epic battle that involves all of Ramona's exes.

Throughout the movie, Scott also has to confront his own personal demons, including his relationship with Knives Chau and his feelings of inadequacy as a musician. In the end, Scott defeats Gideon Graves and wins Ramona's love, but not before realizing that he needs to grow up and become a better person.

The movie features a unique blend of music, action, and comedy, with a distinctive visual style and a memorable soundtrack. The film received widespread critical acclaim for its originality, energy, and performances, and has since become a cult classic among fans of the graphic novel series and action-comedy movies in general.

title: Gifted Hands: The Ben Carson Story
original_title: Gifted Hands: The Ben Carson Story
overview: Gifted Hands: The Ben Carson Story is a movie based on the life story of world-renowned neurosurgeon Ben Carson from 1961 to 1987.
plot:
Gifted Hands: The Ben Carson Story is a 2009 American biographical television film directed by Thomas Carter and written by John Pielmeier, based on the 1990 autobiography of the neurosurgeon Ben Carson, written with Cecil Murphey. Cuba Gooding Jr. stars as Carson, with Kimberly Elise as his mother, Sonya, and Aunjanue Ellis as his wife, Candy. Presented as a Johnson & Johnson Spotlight Presentation, it premiered on TNT on February 7, 2009.

In 1987, Dr. Ben Carson, director of pediatric neurosurgery at Johns Hopkins Hospital, travels to Ulm, West Germany, to meet Peter and Augusta Rausch, whose twin baby boys are joined at the back of the head. He believes the boys could be separated, but warns that the operation risks the lives of one or both. As Carson spends months searching for a way to perform the surgery, the film turns back to his childhood.

In Detroit in 1961, ten-year-old Ben is failing at school and taunted by classmates. His mother, Sonya, a single parent with only a third-grade education, refuses to let her sons fail. She makes Ben and his older brother, Curtis, learn their multiplication tables, limits them to two television programs a week, and requires them to read library books and write reports on them, concealing from the boys that she herself cannot read. Ben discovers a love of books, and within a year he rises from the bottom of his class to the top. As a teenager, however, he struggles with a violent temper, until an incident in which he nearly stabs a friend, whose belt buckle stops the blade. Horrified, Ben prays for forgiveness and finds in his faith the strength to master his anger.

Ben earns a scholarship to Yale University, where he meets his future wife, Candy, and goes on to study medicine. As a neurosurgery resident at Johns Hopkins, he risks his career by operating without supervision to save a dying patient and is rewarded with promotion. In 1985, while Candy suffers the loss of twins in a miscarriage, he performs a hemispherectomy on a young girl suffering from constant seizures, removing half of her brain, and her recovery brings him to public attention.

Back in Germany, Carson finally devises a plan and leads a team through a twenty-two-hour operation that successfully separates the twins, saving both boys' lives, and he faces the press afterward. Gooding was nominated for the Screen Actors Guild Award for his performance, and Carter for a Directors Guild of America Award for his direction.

title: Whiteout
tagline: See Your Last Breath
overview: The only U.S. Marshal assigned to Antarctica, Carrie Stetko will soon leave the harsh environment behind for good – in three days, the sun will set and the Amundsen-Scott Research Station will shut down for the long winter. When a body is discovered out on the open ice, Carrie's investigation into the continent's first homicide plunges her deep into a mystery that may cost her her own life.
plot:
Whiteout is a 2009 crime thriller film directed by Dominic Sena, based on the 1998 comic book series of the same name by Greg Rucka and Steve Lieber. Kate Beckinsale stars as a U.S. Marshal stationed in Antarctica, with Gabriel Macht, Columbus Short and Tom Skerritt. It was produced by Dark Castle Entertainment and distributed by Warner Bros.

In 1957, a Soviet cargo plane flying over Antarctica crashes after a gunfight breaks out aboard over a locked box in its hold. In the present day, Deputy U.S. Marshal Carrie Stetko, who took the post at the Amundsen–Scott South Pole Station two years earlier after a partner's betrayal, is preparing to leave before winter sets in and confides to the station doctor, John Fury, that she intends to resign. Days before the last flight out, a pilot named Delfy reports a body on the ice. The victim, Anton Weiss, one of three scientists searching for meteorites, was murdered with an ice axe, and an autopsy reveals stitches on a leg wound.

Stetko decides to investigate herself. Summoned to the Russian Vostok Station by Weiss's colleague Mooney, she finds him dying and is attacked by a masked man with an ice axe, injuring her hand as she escapes. With Robert Pryce, a United Nations security agent, she comes to suspect the third scientist, Rubin. At the group's search site, Stetko falls through the ice into the wreck of the Soviet plane, where they find the box opened and its canisters missing. Back at the station, Doc amputates two of Stetko's frostbitten fingers. Rubin tells her that he and his colleagues found the plane and took its cargo, but he is killed, and Stetko identifies his murderer as the biologist Russell Haden. As a fierce storm sweeps in and the base is evacuated, Haden escapes and fights Stetko and Pryce outside, until Stetko cuts his safety line and he is carried away by the wind.

Noticing that the stitches on Weiss's leg match those Doc used on her own hand, Stetko opens the wound and finds hidden uncut diamonds, the true cargo of the plane. Doc confesses that he was part of the scientists' scheme to sell them. When he says he wants to see the aurora once more, she lets him walk out into the cold to die. Stetko winters at the station with Pryce and Delfy, and later withdraws her resignation.

Released on September 11, 2009, Whiteout was panned by critics, who found it sluggish and uninspired, and it was a box-office bomb, grossing under $18 million against a $35 million budget.

title: Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs
original_title: Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs
tagline: Prepare to get served.
overview: Inventor Flint Lockwood creates a machine that makes clouds rain food, enabling the down-and-out citizens of Chewandswallow to feed themselves. But when the falling food reaches gargantuan proportions, Flint must scramble to avert disaster. Can he regain control of the machine and put an end to the wild weather before the town is destroyed?
plot:
Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs is a computer-animated comedy film released in 2009 by Columbia Pictures. The movie was directed by Phil Lord and Christopher Miller, and it follows the story of Flint Lockwood, a young inventor who creates a machine that turns water into food.

The movie begins on Swallow Falls Island, where Flint (voiced by Bill Hader) lives with his mother, Linda (voiced by Anna Faris). Flint is a shy and awkward teenager who dreams of becoming a famous weatherman. However, he's constantly overshadowed by the town's eccentric weatherman, Steve the Monkey (voiced by Andy Samberg).

One day, Flint invents a machine called the FLDSMDFR (Flint Lockwood Diatonic Super Mutating Dynamic Food Replicator), which can turn water into food. The machine is initially met with excitement and curiosity, but it quickly gets out of control when it starts producing massive amounts of food that start falling from the sky.

As the town descends into chaos, Flint teams up with Sam Sparks (voiced by Anna Faris), a weather intern who's sent to Swallow Falls to cover the strange weather phenomenon. Together, they try to shut down the machine and restore order to the town.

However, things take a turn when Flint discovers that his invention has attracted the attention of the evil Chester V (voiced by Will Ferrell), a billionaire inventor who wants to use the FLDSMDFR for his own gain. Chester V is determined to capture Flint and harness the power of the machine to create an army of food-dispensing robots.

As the story unfolds, Flint and Sam must navigate through treacherous weather conditions, avoid Chester V's minions, and find a way to shut down the FLDSMDFR before it's too late. Along the way, Flint learns valuable lessons about responsibility, friendship, and following his dreams.

The movie features a talented voice cast, witty humor, and stunning animation that brings the world of Swallow Falls Island to life. The film's climax features an epic battle between Flint and Chester V, with the fate of the town hanging in the balance.

In the end, Flint is able to outsmart Chester V and shut down the FLDSMDFR, saving the town from destruction. The movie concludes on a heartwarming note, with Flint and Sam sharing a romantic moment as the town returns to normal.

Overall, Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs is a delightful animated film that combines humor, adventure, and heart. With its lovable characters, engaging storyline, and stunning animation, it's no wonder why this movie became a beloved classic among both kids and adults alike.

title: Whip It
tagline: Be Your Own Hero
overview: In Bodeen, Texas, Land Of The Dragon, an indie-rock loving misfit finds a way of dealing with her small-town misery after she discovers a roller derby league in nearby Austin.
plot:
Bliss Cavendar is a teenager in the small town of Bodeen, Texas. She has lost interest in the beauty pageants her mother, former beauty queen Brooke, pressures her to win.
While shopping in Austin with her mother, Bliss is intrigued by three roller derby team members she encounters. She and her friend Pash attend a roller derby bout where they see the "Holy Rollers" defeat the "Hurl Scouts". Bliss lies about her age and tries out for the Hurl Scouts, who give her the derby name "Babe Ruthless", and she becomes friendly with teammates "Maggie Mayhem", "Bloody Holly" and "Smashley Simpson". The Hurl Scouts, while enthusiastic and close knit, rarely win, but chant, "We're number two!" after losing a match, to the frustration of their coach, Razor.
"Iron Maven" of the Holy Rollers resents Bliss's talent and youth. Bliss soon realizes she needs to be merciless in roller derby, which also changes other aspects of her life. She stands up to a bully at school and starts dating a lanky musician named Oliver, to whom she loses her virginity before he leaves on a tour, taking a T-shirt Bliss gave him to remember her by, in exchange for his jacket.
The Hurl Scouts continue to lose. Razor convinces them to change their ways after paying their rivals to use one of his plays against them, showing them how much better they could be. The team begins rising in the ranks, soon heading for a championship match against the Holy Rollers.
Bliss's parents discover her involvement in roller derby when Pash is arrested at the arena for underage drinking. Pash is furious with Bliss for leaving her alone, which led to her arrest. When Bliss's parents demand she give up roller derby, she runs away from home and stays with Maggie, discovering she has a young son. Maggie gives Bliss perspective on the difficulties of being a parent.
Bliss sees a picture of Oliver on social media with another girl, who is wearing her t-shirt. Heartbroken, she goes home to her mother, who comforts her. Bliss gives up roller derby and resumes her pageant career so as not to hurt her family or friends any further, and reconciles with Pash.
On the day of the pageant, which is the same day as the roller derby championship, Bliss's father convinces his wife to let Bliss abandon the pageant and go join the Hurl Scouts in their championship game.
Before the game begins, Bliss is approached by Oliver, who denies cheating on her, but she dumps him anyway for never calling her while he was away. The Hurl Scouts narrowly lose the championship match to the Holy Rollers, but they still happily come together and chant, "We're number two!" She and Iron Maven come to a mutual respect. Bliss's mother is still not entirely supportive of roller derby, but accepts that Bliss now knows what makes her happy and is charting her own course in life.

title: Law Abiding Citizen
tagline: Justice at any cost.
overview: A frustrated man decides to take justice into his own hands after a plea bargain sets one of his family's killers free. He targets not only the killer but also the district attorney and others involved in the deal.
plot:
Law Abiding Citizen is a 2009 American vigilante action thriller film directed by F. Gary Gray and written by Kurt Wimmer. Set in Philadelphia, it stars Gerard Butler as Clyde Shelton, a man who wages war on the justice system after one of his family's killers receives a lenient plea deal, and Jamie Foxx as the prosecutor Nick Rice, with Bruce McGill, Colm Meaney, Leslie Bibb, Regina Hall, Michael Irby, Christian Stolte and Josh Stewart.

When two burglars, Rupert Ames and Clarence Darby, invade Clyde's home, Darby stabs him and rapes and murders his wife and daughter. Prosecutor Nick Rice, unwilling to risk his high conviction rate on weak evidence, ignores Clyde's pleas and lets Darby plead guilty to third-degree murder for a three-year sentence in exchange for testifying against Ames, who is sentenced to death. Ten years later, Ames's execution goes horribly wrong because the drugs have been replaced. Disguised as a police officer, Clyde paralyzes Darby with a toxin-laced trap and records himself torturing him to death. Arrested, he mails the recording to Nick's daughter and, representing himself, berates the judge who approved Darby's deal, who then denies him bail.

From his cell, Clyde trades confessions for luxuries, and when Nick misses a deadline, Darby's lawyer is found buried alive. Clyde kills his cellmate and is put in solitary confinement. A CIA contact reveals that he was once an agency specialist in unconventional assassinations. Clyde says that he is exposing the failures of the justice system, and the killings continue: the judge dies when her phone explodes, Nick's assistant and colleagues die in car bombings, and the district attorney is killed by an armed robot. Promoted to acting district attorney, Nick learns that Clyde owns a building near the prison, where he and a detective find a tunnel leading to the solitary cells, revealing that Clyde has been slipping out undetected. Clyde plants a napalm bomb beneath a City Hall emergency meeting, but it has been moved under Clyde's bed, and Clyde dies clutching his daughter's bracelet when he triggers it. Nick finally attends his daughter's cello recital.

Released on October 16, 2009, the film opened second at the box office and grossed about $127 million worldwide. Reviews were generally negative; critics praised the premise and central performances but criticized the logic, violence and moral stance, and Rotten Tomatoes gave it 26% approval.
